questions.questionEn: According to the BC Patient Assessment Model, which sequence correctly lists the seven components in their standard order?
questions.questionZh: 根据 BC Patient Assessment Model，下列哪一项正确列出了七个组成部分的标准顺序？

options.en: Primary Survey, Rescue Scene Evaluation, Secondary Survey, Treatments, Protocols, Load and Transport, Records and Reports
options.zh: Primary Survey、Rescue Scene Evaluation、Secondary Survey、Treatments、Protocols、Load and Transport、Records and Reports

options.en: Rescue Scene Evaluation, Primary Survey, Secondary Survey, Protocols, Treatments, Load and Transport, Records and Reports
options.zh: Rescue Scene Evaluation、Primary Survey、Secondary Survey、Protocols、Treatments、Load and Transport、Records and Reports

options.en: Rescue Scene Evaluation, Secondary Survey, Primary Survey, Protocols, Treatments, Records and Reports, Load and Transport
options.zh: Rescue Scene Evaluation、Secondary Survey、Primary Survey、Protocols、Treatments、Records and Reports、Load and Transport

options.en: Primary Survey, Secondary Survey, Rescue Scene Evaluation, Load and Transport, Protocols, Treatments, Records and Reports
options.zh: Primary Survey、Secondary Survey、Rescue Scene Evaluation、Load and Transport、Protocols、Treatments、Records and Reports

questions.explanationEn: The model on p.6 flows: Rescue Scene Evaluation, Primary Survey, Secondary Survey (history, vital signs, head-to-toe), Protocols, Treatments, Load and Transport, then Records and Reports. Depending on stability, load and transport may move up any time after the decision point, but this is the generic order.
questions.explanationZh: p.6 的模型顺序为：Rescue Scene Evaluation → Primary Survey → Secondary Survey（history、vital signs、head-to-toe）→ Protocols → Treatments → Load and Transport → Records and Reports。依据病人稳定程度，load and transport 可以在 decision point 之后随时提前，但通用顺序如上。

questions.questionEn: You arrive at a single-vehicle MVA at night. The car has struck a power pole and a wire is draped across the hood. The driver is slumped over the wheel. What should you do first?
questions.questionZh: 夜间你到达一起单车 MVA 现场。汽车撞上电线杆，一根电线搭在引擎盖上，驾驶员趴在方向盘上。你首先应该做什么？

options.en: Approach the driver's window and begin the primary survey through the glass
options.zh: 走近驾驶员车窗，隔着玻璃开始 primary survey

options.en: Instruct the driver to open the door and step away from the vehicle
options.zh: 指示驾驶员打开车门并离开车辆

options.en: Stage at a safe distance and confirm the line is de-energized by the utility crew before anyone approaches
options.zh: 在安全距离外待命，等电力公司确认电线断电后再让任何人接近

options.en: Move the wire off the hood with a wooden pole so you can access the patient
options.zh: 用木杆把电线从引擎盖上挑开以便接触病人

questions.explanationEn: Hazard identification is the first step of the Rescue Scene Evaluation, and the electrical contact guideline is explicit: do not approach electrical sources or downed power lines until qualified personnel have deemed the scene safe. No patient contact or instruction to exit occurs until the scene is cleared.
questions.explanationZh: Hazards 是 Rescue Scene Evaluation 的第一步，而 electrical contact 指南明确要求：在合格人员确认现场安全之前，不得接近电源或落地电线。现场未清除危险前不能接触病人，也不能指示其下车。

questions.questionEn: What is the stated purpose of the primary survey in the BC Patient Assessment Model?
questions.questionZh: 在 BC Patient Assessment Model 中，primary survey 的明确目的（purpose）是什么？

options.en: To identify and manage life- and limb-threatening injuries and conditions
options.zh: 识别并处理危及生命和肢体的损伤与病情

options.en: To establish a baseline set of vital signs and identify the chief complaint
options.zh: 建立基线 vital signs 并确定 chief complaint

options.en: To ensure the scene is safe for the crew and the patient
options.zh: 确保现场对救护人员和病人安全

options.en: To gather a complete SAMPLE history before treatment begins
options.zh: 在治疗开始前收集完整的 SAMPLE history

questions.explanationEn: Per the component table, the primary survey exists to identify and manage life- and limb-threatening injuries and conditions. Baseline vitals and chief complaint belong to the secondary survey; scene safety is the purpose of the Rescue Scene Evaluation.
questions.explanationZh: 根据组件表，primary survey 的目的是识别并处理危及生命和肢体的损伤与病情。基线 vitals 和 chief complaint 属于 secondary survey；现场安全是 Rescue Scene Evaluation 的目的。

questions.questionEn: Which element of the secondary survey is specifically listed in the BC guidelines as required at the PCP level?
questions.questionZh: BC 指南中，secondary survey 的哪个组成部分被特别标注为 PCP 级别必须完成（required）？

options.en: Head-to-toe examination
options.zh: Head-to-toe examination（从头到脚检查）

options.en: Baseline vital signs
options.zh: 基线 vital signs

options.en: History taking
options.zh: History（病史采集）

options.en: Functional inquiry
options.zh: Functional inquiry（系统回顾问诊）

questions.explanationEn: The secondary survey consists of history, vital signs, head-to-toe examination, and functional inquiry, with functional inquiry annotated as PCP required. History, vitals, and head-to-toe are expected at all licence levels.
questions.explanationZh: Secondary survey 包括 history、vital signs、head-to-toe examination 和 functional inquiry，其中 functional inquiry 标注为 PCP required。History、vitals 和 head-to-toe 是所有级别都要完成的。

questions.questionEn: A 24-year-old man has been stabbed in the left chest. Your primary survey finds respiratory distress with accessory muscle use and a sealed open chest wound. He is clearly unstable. What is the most appropriate next step?
questions.questionZh: 一名 24 岁男性左胸被刺伤。Primary survey 发现呼吸窘迫伴辅助呼吸肌使用，开放性胸部伤口已封闭。他明显不稳定。下一步最合适的做法是什么？

options.en: Complete a full head-to-toe examination on scene before moving him
options.zh: 搬动前先在现场完成完整的 head-to-toe examination

options.en: Load and initiate transport now, completing the secondary survey en route
options.zh: 立即装载并开始转运，在途中完成 secondary survey

options.en: Obtain a full SAMPLE history and two sets of vital signs on scene
options.zh: 在现场完成完整 SAMPLE history 和两组 vital signs

options.en: Wait on scene for ALS intercept before any movement
options.zh: 在现场等待 ALS 支援后再搬动病人

questions.explanationEn: The model's footnote states that depending on patient condition (stable vs unstable), load and transport may be appropriate any time after the decision point. Major penetrating torso trauma with respiratory distress is unstable: transport is prioritized and the secondary survey continues en route.
questions.explanationZh: 模型脚注指出：依据病人情况（stable vs unstable），load and transport 可以在 decision point 之后随时进行。胸部大穿透伤伴呼吸窘迫属于不稳定：应优先转运，secondary survey 在途中继续完成。

questions.questionEn: You find a 30-year-old man lying on a couch after a party. He does not respond when you enter, but when you loudly call his name he opens his eyes, mumbles an answer, and drifts back off. On the AVPU scale he is:
questions.questionZh: 派对后你发现一名 30 岁男性躺在沙发上。你进门时他没有反应，但当你大声喊他名字时，他睁眼、含糊地应了一声，然后又昏睡过去。按 AVPU 评分他属于：

options.en: V - he responds to verbal stimulus but is drowsy; consider placing him semi-prone if injuries permit
options.zh: V —— 对言语刺激有反应但嗜睡；如损伤允许可考虑摆 semi-prone 体位

options.en: A - he is alert because he answered a question appropriately
options.zh: A —— 他能回答问题，所以属于 alert

options.en: P - he required a loud stimulus, which counts as a painful stimulus
options.zh: P —— 需要大声刺激才有反应，等同于疼痛刺激

options.en: U - he is unresponsive because he keeps drifting back to sleep
options.zh: U —— 他持续昏睡，属于 unresponsive

questions.explanationEn: A patient who responds to verbal stimulus but is drowsy is V on the AVPU scale. The guideline notes such a patient may be considered for semi-prone positioning if injuries permit, because a decreased LOC threatens the airway. A loud voice is still a verbal stimulus, not pain.
questions.explanationZh: 对言语刺激有反应但嗜睡的病人在 AVPU 中评为 V。指南提示：如损伤允许，可考虑 semi-prone 体位，因为意识下降会威胁气道。大声呼喊仍属言语刺激而非疼痛刺激。

questions.questionEn: A warehouse worker is found unconscious on the floor at the base of a storage rack. Nobody saw what happened. There are no obvious injuries. Regarding cervical spine stabilization, you should:
questions.questionZh: 一名仓库工人被发现昏迷倒在货架底下的地面上，无人目击事发经过，没有明显外伤。关于颈椎固定，你应该：

options.en: Defer spinal precautions because there are no visible injuries above the clavicles
options.zh: 因为锁骨以上没有可见损伤，暂不做脊柱保护

options.en: Apply spinal precautions only if he wakes up and reports neck pain
options.zh: 只有当他醒来并主诉颈痛时才做脊柱保护

options.en: Clear the spine using NEXUS criteria since he cannot report pain
options.zh: 既然他无法主诉疼痛，就用 NEXUS 标准来排除颈椎损伤

options.en: Stabilize the cervical spine because he is unconscious and trauma cannot be reasonably ruled out
options.zh: 进行颈椎固定，因为他处于昏迷状态且无法合理排除外伤

questions.explanationEn: Primary survey intervention indications for cervical spine stabilization include an unconscious patient where trauma cannot be reasonably ruled out. An unwitnessed collapse beside a storage rack could involve a fall or struck-by mechanism, so precautions apply. NEXUS cannot be applied to an unassessable patient.
questions.explanationZh: Primary survey 干预中，颈椎固定的指征包括：昏迷且无法合理排除外伤的病人。货架旁无目击的倒地可能涉及坠落或被砸的机制，故应做脊柱保护。NEXUS 标准无法用于不能配合评估的病人。

questions.questionEn: During the rapid body survey of a stabbing victim you discover a bubbling open wound on the right chest. The airway is clear and breathing is laboured. What should you do about the wound?
questions.questionZh: 在对一名刺伤病人做 rapid body survey 时，你发现右胸有一个冒泡的开放性伤口。气道通畅，呼吸费力。对这个伤口你应该怎么处理？

options.en: Note its location and seal it during the treatment component after the secondary survey
options.zh: 记录位置，等 secondary survey 之后的 treatment 阶段再封闭

options.en: Pack the wound with hemostatic gauze to stop air entry
options.zh: 用止血纱布填塞伤口以阻止空气进入

options.en: Seal it immediately as a primary survey intervention, then continue the survey
options.zh: 立即封闭伤口——这是 primary survey 干预之一——然后继续检查

options.en: Leave it open so air can escape and prevent a tension pneumothorax
options.zh: 保持开放让空气逸出，以预防张力性气胸

questions.explanationEn: Sealing open chest wounds is listed as a primary survey intervention: life-threatening findings are managed as they are found. Do not pack wounds on the chest. Sealing uses a three-sided occlusive dressing or commercial chest seal, then the survey continues while monitoring for tension pneumothorax.
questions.explanationZh: 封闭开放性胸部伤口是 primary survey 干预之一：发现威胁生命的问题就立即处理。胸部伤口禁止填塞。应使用三边封闭敷料或商用 chest seal 封闭，然后继续检查并监测张力性气胸。

questions.questionEn: A 35-year-old roofer fell approximately 7 meters onto grass. He is alert, complaining only of left wrist pain, with strong radial pulses and normal breathing. How should he be categorized for transport?
questions.questionZh: 一名 35 岁屋顶工从约 7 米高处坠落到草地上。他神志清楚，只主诉左腕疼痛，桡动脉搏动有力，呼吸正常。转运分类应如何判断？

options.en: Stable, because his primary survey shows no life-threatening findings
options.zh: 稳定——因为 primary survey 没有危及生命的发现

options.en: Unstable and transported appropriately, because a free fall from over 6 meters is a high-risk mechanism
options.zh: 不稳定并按不稳定转运——因为超过 6 米的自由坠落属于高危机制

options.en: Stable, because the landing surface was soft grass
options.zh: 稳定——因为落地面是柔软的草地

options.en: Unstable only if his vital signs deteriorate during the secondary survey
options.zh: 只有当 secondary survey 中 vitals 恶化时才算不稳定

questions.explanationEn: Mechanism of injury alone can classify a patient as unstable: a free fall from a height greater than 6 meters (about 20 feet) is on the list. Reassuring initial findings do not remove the mechanism-based risk of occult internal injury.
questions.explanationZh: 仅凭受伤机制即可判定不稳定：超过 6 米（约 20 英尺）的自由坠落在清单之列。初始表现良好并不能消除机制带来的隐匿性内伤风险。

questions.questionEn: You attend a two-vehicle MVA. Your patient is the restrained driver, GCS 15, vitals normal, complaining of chest soreness from the seatbelt. The front-seat passenger of the same vehicle was pronounced dead at the scene. Your transport decision is based on:
questions.questionZh: 你处理一起两车相撞的 MVA。你的病人是系了安全带的驾驶员，GCS 15，vitals 正常，主诉安全带造成的胸部酸痛。同车前排乘客已当场宣告死亡。你的转运决策依据是：

options.en: Stable - his own examination findings are normal
options.zh: 稳定——他本人的检查结果正常

options.en: Stable - the death of another occupant only matters if the patient was also ejected
options.zh: 稳定——除非病人也被甩出车外，否则他人死亡不影响分类

options.en: Unstable only if compartment intrusion exceeded 0.5 m on his side
options.zh: 只有当他这一侧车厢侵入超过 0.5 米时才算不稳定

options.en: Unstable - a death in the same passenger compartment is a high-risk mechanism criterion
options.zh: 不稳定——同一乘员舱内有死亡是高危机制标准之一

questions.explanationEn: Death in the passenger compartment is listed under high-risk automobile crash mechanisms. It indicates the forces involved were severe enough to kill, so surviving occupants are managed as unstable regardless of initial presentation. Intrusion criteria (>0.3 m occupant side) are separate, additional triggers.
questions.explanationZh: 同一乘员舱内有死亡是高危车祸机制标准之一。它说明碰撞能量足以致死，因此幸存乘员无论初始表现如何都按不稳定处理。车厢侵入（乘员侧 >0.3 米）是另一条独立标准。

questions.questionEn: A 28-year-old cyclist was struck by a car travelling approximately 40 km/h. She is alert with abrasions and a deformed left forearm, vitals within normal limits. What is the correct transport categorization?
questions.questionZh: 一名 28 岁骑自行车者被一辆时速约 40 km/h 的汽车撞倒。她神志清楚，有擦伤和左前臂畸形，vitals 在正常范围。正确的转运分类是什么？

options.en: Unstable - auto versus cyclist at greater than 30 km/h is a high-risk mechanism
options.zh: 不稳定——汽车撞骑车人且车速超过 30 km/h 属于高危机制

options.en: Stable - an isolated forearm fracture is not a proximal long bone injury
options.zh: 稳定——孤立前臂骨折不属于近端长骨损伤

options.en: Stable - she would only be unstable if thrown more than 6 meters
options.zh: 稳定——只有被抛出超过 6 米才算不稳定

options.en: Unstable only if she lost consciousness at the scene
options.zh: 只有当她现场曾意识丧失时才算不稳定

questions.explanationEn: Auto versus pedestrian or cyclist at greater than 30 km/h is a listed high-risk mechanism, making her unstable for transport purposes even though her anatomical injuries appear limited. The forearm fracture is managed, but the mechanism drives the decision.
questions.explanationZh: 汽车撞行人/骑车人且车速超过 30 km/h 属于高危机制清单内容，即使她的解剖学损伤看起来有限，也应按不稳定转运。前臂骨折照常处理，但转运决策由机制决定。

questions.questionEn: In a parking lot, a reversing car bumped a 40-year-old pedestrian at roughly 10-15 km/h. He was knocked down but did not lose consciousness. Primary survey is unremarkable; he has a small scalp abrasion and normal vitals. The best decision is:
questions.questionZh: 停车场里，一辆倒车的汽车以大约 10-15 km/h 的速度碰倒了一名 40 岁行人。他被撞倒但没有意识丧失。Primary survey 无异常，只有头皮小擦伤，vitals 正常。最佳决策是：

options.en: Rapid transport - any auto versus pedestrian collision is automatically a high-risk mechanism
options.zh: 快速转运——任何汽车撞行人都自动属于高危机制

options.en: Rapid transport - a scalp wound counts as major penetrating trauma to the head
options.zh: 快速转运——头皮伤口算作头部大穿透伤

options.en: Complete the full assessment on scene; the mechanism threshold of over 30 km/h is not met and no unstable findings are present
options.zh: 在现场完成完整评估；未达到超过 30 km/h 的机制门槛，也没有不稳定表现

options.en: No transport is needed because the impact speed was low
options.zh: 因为撞击速度低，不需要转运

questions.explanationEn: The mechanism criterion is auto versus pedestrian at greater than 30 km/h; a low-speed parking-lot bump does not meet it. With no unstable primary survey or anatomical findings, he is assessed fully on scene and transported routinely. Low speed does not mean no assessment or no transport - he still warrants evaluation.
questions.explanationZh: 机制标准是汽车撞行人且车速超过 30 km/h；停车场低速碰撞未达门槛。Primary survey 与解剖学检查均无不稳定发现时，应在现场完成完整评估后常规转运。低速不等于不需要评估或转运——他仍需要就医检查。

questions.questionEn: Which of the following anatomical findings places an adult trauma patient in the unstable category under the BC guidelines?
questions.questionZh: 根据 BC 指南，下列哪一项解剖学发现会将成人创伤病人归入不稳定类别？

options.en: A closed fracture of one wrist with intact distal circulation
options.zh: 单侧腕部闭合骨折，远端循环完好

options.en: Fractures of both femurs
options.zh: 双侧股骨骨折

options.en: A partial thickness burn covering 10% of body surface area on the back
options.zh: 背部 10% 体表面积的部分皮层烧伤

options.en: A single rib fracture with equal air entry
options.zh: 单根肋骨骨折，双侧进气均等

questions.explanationEn: Two or more proximal long bone fractures is a listed anatomical instability criterion; bilateral femur fractures meet it and also carry major hemorrhage risk. A wrist fracture, partial thickness burn of 10% BSA (threshold is >20%), and single rib fracture without instability do not meet the criteria.
questions.explanationZh: 两处及以上近端长骨骨折是解剖学不稳定标准之一；双侧股骨骨折符合，且伴有大出血风险。腕部骨折、10% BSA 的部分皮层烧伤（门槛是 >20%）和无胸壁不稳的单根肋骨骨折都不符合标准。

questions.questionEn: A 45-year-old carpenter amputated his thumb with a table saw. Bleeding is controlled with a pressure dressing, he is calm, and vitals are normal. Which statement about his management is correct?
questions.questionZh: 一名 45 岁木工被台锯切断拇指。压力敷料已控制出血，他情绪平稳，vitals 正常。关于处理，下列哪项正确？

options.en: He is unstable because any amputation is an anatomical instability criterion
options.zh: 他不稳定——任何截肢都属于解剖学不稳定标准

options.en: The thumb should be placed directly on ice to maximize viability
options.zh: 拇指应直接放在冰上以最大限度保存活性

options.en: He requires a tourniquet regardless of whether direct pressure controlled the bleed
options.zh: 无论直接压迫是否已止血，都必须上止血带

options.en: He does not meet the instability criterion - that applies to amputations proximal to the wrist or ankle - so manage the wound, preserve the part, and transport
options.zh: 他不符合不稳定标准——该标准针对腕/踝以近的截肢——处理伤口、保存断指、常规转运即可

questions.explanationEn: The anatomical criterion is amputation proximal to the wrist or ankle; a thumb amputation with controlled hemorrhage does not meet it. The part is rinsed with cool sterile water, wrapped in saline-moistened gauze, bagged, kept cool (never directly on ice), and transported with the patient.
questions.explanationZh: 解剖学标准是腕或踝以近的截肢；出血已控制的拇指截肢不符合。断指应以凉的无菌水冲洗、用生理盐水湿润纱布松裹、装袋后保持低温（绝不可直接放冰上），随病人一起转运。

questions.questionEn: A welder has a full thickness burn that completely encircles his right forearm, estimated at 5% BSA. He is alert with normal vitals and severe pain. How is he categorized?
questions.questionZh: 一名焊工右前臂被全层烧伤，烧伤环绕整个前臂一圈，估计 5% BSA。他神志清楚，vitals 正常，疼痛剧烈。他应如何分类？

options.en: Unstable - burns that fully encircle a limb are a listed criterion regardless of BSA
options.zh: 不稳定——环绕肢体一整圈的烧伤是明确标准之一，与 BSA 无关

options.en: Stable - full thickness burns only count when they exceed 10% BSA
options.zh: 稳定——全层烧伤只有超过 10% BSA 才算

options.en: Stable - the burn does not involve the face, hands, or airway
options.zh: 稳定——烧伤不涉及面部、手或气道

options.en: Unstable only if distal pulses are already absent
options.zh: 只有当远端脉搏已消失时才算不稳定

questions.explanationEn: Burns that fully encircle a limb appear on the major burns list independent of the BSA percentage thresholds, because circumferential burns can act like a tourniquet as edema develops. Waiting for pulses to disappear would mean waiting for the complication to occur.
questions.explanationZh: 环绕肢体一圈的烧伤独立列于 major burns 标准中，与 BSA 百分比门槛无关，因为环形烧伤随水肿进展可产生类似止血带的效应。等远端脉搏消失才升级，等于等并发症发生。

questions.questionEn: Which primary survey finding places an adult patient in the unstable category for examination purposes?
questions.questionZh: 以下哪个 primary survey 发现会使成人病人被归为不稳定（考试标准）？

options.en: Heart rate of 96 with warm, dry skin
options.zh: 心率 96，皮肤温暖干燥

options.en: Localized abdominal tenderness with normal vitals
options.zh: 局限性腹部压痛，vitals 正常

options.en: Absent radial pulses
options.zh: 桡动脉搏动消失

options.en: Pain rated 8 out of 10 from an isolated ankle injury
options.zh: 孤立踝部损伤，疼痛评分 8/10

questions.explanationEn: Absent radial pulses appear on the primary survey instability list - they suggest significant hypotension or peripheral shutdown from shock. Tachycardia alone with good skin, localized tenderness, or severe pain from a minor injury do not by themselves meet the listed criteria.
questions.explanationZh: 桡动脉搏动消失在 primary survey 不稳定清单中——提示明显低血压或休克导致的外周灌注关闭。单纯轻度心率增快伴皮肤良好、局限性压痛、或小伤口的剧烈疼痛本身都不在清单标准内。

questions.questionEn: A 40-year-old fell from a ladder. He opens his eyes when you speak to him, is confused about where he is and the date, and follows your command to squeeze your fingers. What is his GCS and injury classification?
questions.questionZh: 一名 40 岁男性从梯子上摔下。你和他说话时他会睁眼，对地点和日期表述混乱（confused），但能按指令握你的手指。他的 GCS 是多少？属于哪一级损伤？

options.en: GCS 11 - moderate traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 11 —— 中度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: GCS 13 - mild traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 13 —— 轻度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: GCS 15 - no brain injury
options.zh: GCS 15 —— 无脑损伤

options.en: GCS 9 - moderate traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 9 —— 中度创伤性脑损伤

questions.explanationEn: Eye opening to voice scores 3, confused speech scores 4, obeying commands scores 6: total GCS 13. Per the guideline, a GCS of 13 or higher indicates mild traumatic brain injury. Note that confused but converses is V4, not V3 (inappropriate words).
questions.explanationZh: 呼唤睁眼 E3，言语混乱 V4，遵嘱动作 M6，合计 GCS 13。按指南，GCS ≥ 13 提示轻度创伤性脑损伤。注意「混乱但能对话」是 V4，而不是 V3（不恰当言语）。

questions.questionEn: An assault victim opens his eyes only to a trapezius squeeze, makes incomprehensible moaning sounds, and withdraws his arm from the painful stimulus. What is his GCS and classification?
questions.questionZh: 一名被殴打的伤者只有在斜方肌掐捏时才睁眼，发出无法理解的呻吟声，并会从疼痛刺激中回缩手臂。他的 GCS 和分级是什么？

options.en: GCS 10 - moderate traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 10 —— 中度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: GCS 6 - severe traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 6 —— 重度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: GCS 9 - moderate traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 9 —— 中度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: GCS 8 - severe traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 8 —— 重度创伤性脑损伤

questions.explanationEn: Eye opening to pain scores 2, incomprehensible sounds score 2, withdrawal from pain scores 4: total GCS 8. A GCS of 8 or less is defined as severe traumatic brain injury, with implications for aggressive airway monitoring and rapid transport.
questions.explanationZh: 疼痛刺激睁眼 E2，无法理解的声音 V2，疼痛回缩 M4，合计 GCS 8。GCS ≤ 8 定义为重度创伤性脑损伤，意味着需要严密的气道管理和快速转运。

questions.questionEn: Following a motorcycle crash, a rider has no eye opening to any stimulus, makes no sounds, and extends both arms rigidly when a painful stimulus is applied. What is his GCS?
questions.questionZh: 摩托车事故后，一名骑手对任何刺激均不睁眼、不发声，疼痛刺激时双臂僵硬伸直（extension）。他的 GCS 是多少？

options.en: GCS 4
options.zh: GCS 4

options.en: GCS 3
options.zh: GCS 3

options.en: GCS 6
options.zh: GCS 6

options.en: GCS 5
options.zh: GCS 5

questions.explanationEn: No eye opening scores 1, no verbal response scores 1, and extension to pain scores 2, totalling GCS 4 - a severe traumatic brain injury. Extension (decerebrate) scores 2 while abnormal flexion (decorticate) scores 3; confusing the two is a common exam error. The minimum possible GCS is 3, not 0.
questions.explanationZh: 不睁眼 E1，无言语 V1，疼痛刺激伸直（去大脑强直）M2，合计 GCS 4，属重度创伤性脑损伤。伸直（decerebrate）计 2 分，异常屈曲（decorticate）计 3 分，两者混淆是常见考试错误。GCS 最低分是 3 而不是 0。

questions.questionEn: According to the BC guidelines, a Glasgow Coma Scale score between 9 and 12 after head trauma suggests which classification?
questions.questionZh: 根据 BC 指南，头部外伤后 GCS 在 9 到 12 之间提示哪一级损伤？

options.en: Mild traumatic brain injury
options.zh: 轻度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: Severe traumatic brain injury
options.zh: 重度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: Moderate traumatic brain injury
options.zh: 中度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: No traumatic brain injury
options.zh: 无创伤性脑损伤

questions.explanationEn: The guideline classifies GCS 13 or greater as mild, 9 to 12 as moderate, and 8 or less as severe traumatic brain injury. These bands guide airway vigilance, oxygenation targets (SpO2 at least 94%), and transport urgency.
questions.explanationZh: 指南将 GCS ≥ 13 归为轻度，9-12 为中度，≤ 8 为重度创伤性脑损伤。该分级指导气道警戒、氧合目标（SpO2 ≥ 94%）与转运紧迫性。

questions.questionEn: A 33-year-old with a lacerated thigh has these serial vitals - on arrival: HR 92, BP 128/84, RR 18, skin warm; 15 minutes later: HR 118, BP 96/72, RR 24, skin cool and pale. What do these trends indicate?
questions.questionZh: 一名 33 岁大腿裂伤病人的连续 vitals：到达时 HR 92、BP 128/84、RR 18、皮肤温暖；15 分钟后 HR 118、BP 96/72、RR 24、皮肤湿冷苍白。这个趋势提示什么？

options.en: Anxiety response - the falling BP reflects the patient calming down
options.zh: 焦虑反应——血压下降说明病人逐渐平静

options.en: Progressing hemorrhagic shock - he is now unstable and requires rapid transport with hemorrhage control
options.zh: 失血性休克进展——他已属不稳定，需要止血并快速转运

options.en: Normal variation - both readings are within acceptable adult ranges
options.zh: 正常波动——两组读数都在成人可接受范围内

options.en: Improving perfusion because the heart is compensating effectively
options.zh: 灌注改善——因为心脏正在有效代偿

questions.explanationEn: Rising heart rate and respiratory rate with falling blood pressure and deteriorating skin signs is the classic trajectory of decompensating hemorrhagic shock. Cool pale clammy skin secondary to suspected shock is itself an unstable primary survey finding. Single readings can mislead; trends tell the story.
questions.explanationZh: 心率和呼吸频率上升、血压下降、皮肤征象恶化，是失血性休克失代偿的典型轨迹。疑似休克导致的湿冷苍白皮肤本身就是 primary survey 的不稳定表现之一。单次读数会误导，趋势才能说明问题。

questions.questionEn: A 26-year-old struck his head snowboarding. During transport his BP climbs from 130/76 to 172/60, his heart rate falls from 88 to 54, and his respirations become irregular. His right pupil is now sluggish. This pattern most likely represents:
questions.questionZh: 一名 26 岁男子滑雪板时撞到头部。转运途中血压从 130/76 升到 172/60，心率从 88 降到 54，呼吸变得不规则，右侧瞳孔反应迟钝。这种组合最可能代表：

options.en: Hypovolemic shock from an associated internal bleed
options.zh: 合并内出血导致的低血容量性休克

options.en: A normal vagal response to pain and anxiety
options.zh: 疼痛和焦虑引起的正常迷走反应

options.en: Early anaphylaxis from an unknown exposure
options.zh: 不明暴露引起的早期过敏性休克

options.en: Rising intracranial pressure - reassess ABCs, support oxygenation to SpO2 of at least 94%, and notify the receiving facility
options.zh: 颅内压升高——重新评估 ABC，维持 SpO2 ≥ 94%，并通知接收医院

questions.explanationEn: Rising blood pressure with widening pulse pressure, bradycardia, and irregular respirations is the Cushing response to rising intracranial pressure - the opposite of hypovolemic shock, where BP falls and HR rises. Management follows the TBI guideline: oxygenation at SpO2 of 94% or above, head of bed elevated 30 degrees, loosened collar, and early notification.
questions.explanationZh: 血压升高伴脉压增宽、心动过缓和不规则呼吸是颅内压升高的 Cushing 反应——与低血容量性休克（血压降、心率升）正好相反。处理遵循 TBI 指南：维持 SpO2 ≥ 94%、床头抬高 30 度、松开硬质颈托、尽早通知医院。

questions.questionEn: You are asked to infuse 500 mL of normal saline over 12 hours using a macro-drip set rated at 10 gtts/mL. What drip rate should you set?
questions.questionZh: 需要用 10 gtts/mL 的 macro-drip 输液器在 12 小时内输入 500 mL 生理盐水。滴速应设为多少？

options.en: 7 gtts/min
options.zh: 7 gtts/min

options.en: 12 gtts/min
options.zh: 12 gtts/min

options.en: 25 gtts/min
options.zh: 25 gtts/min

options.en: 42 gtts/min
options.zh: 42 gtts/min

questions.explanationEn: gtts per minute = volume x set rate / time in minutes = 500 x 10 / 720 = 5000 / 720 = approximately 7 gtts/min. This is the worked example in the guideline. Choosing 42 would be the error of using a 60 gtts/mL micro-drip factor.
questions.explanationZh: gtts/min = 容量 x 输液器滴系数 / 分钟数 = 500 x 10 / 720 = 5000 / 720 ≈ 7 gtts/min。这正是指南中的例题。选 42 是误用了 60 gtts/mL micro-drip 系数的结果。

questions.questionEn: You must infuse 25 mL of D10W over 60 minutes using a micro-drip set (60 gtts/mL). What is the correct drip rate?
questions.questionZh: 需要用 micro-drip 输液器（60 gtts/mL）在 60 分钟内输入 25 mL D10W。正确滴速是多少？

options.en: 4 gtts/min
options.zh: 4 gtts/min

options.en: 15 gtts/min
options.zh: 15 gtts/min

options.en: 25 gtts/min
options.zh: 25 gtts/min

options.en: 60 gtts/min
options.zh: 60 gtts/min

questions.explanationEn: 25 mL x 60 gtts/mL / 60 minutes = 1500 / 60 = 25 gtts/min. This matches the guideline's second worked example. A convenient rule: with a 60 gtts/mL micro-drip set, gtts/min equals mL/hr.
questions.explanationZh: 25 mL x 60 gtts/mL / 60 分钟 = 1500 / 60 = 25 gtts/min，与指南第二个例题一致。速记：使用 60 gtts/mL micro-drip 时，gtts/min 数值等于 mL/hr。

questions.questionEn: A physician orders 1000 mL of normal saline over 6 hours during a long transfer. Your set delivers 10 gtts/mL. What drip rate do you run?
questions.questionZh: 长途转运中医嘱要求 6 小时输入 1000 mL 生理盐水。你的输液器为 10 gtts/mL。滴速应是多少？

options.en: 17 gtts/min
options.zh: 17 gtts/min

options.en: 28 gtts/min
options.zh: 28 gtts/min

options.en: 42 gtts/min
options.zh: 42 gtts/min

options.en: 167 gtts/min
options.zh: 167 gtts/min

questions.explanationEn: 1000 mL x 10 gtts/mL / 360 minutes = 10000 / 360 = approximately 28 gtts/min. Answer 167 is the micro-drip error (60 gtts/mL); 17 comes from mistakenly using 10 hours.
questions.explanationZh: 1000 mL x 10 gtts/mL / 360 分钟 = 10000 / 360 ≈ 28 gtts/min。选 167 是误用 micro-drip（60 gtts/mL）；选 17 是把时间错算成 10 小时。

questions.questionEn: En route, you need to infuse 100 mL of normal saline over 30 minutes using a 10 gtts/mL set. What drip rate should you run?
questions.questionZh: 转运途中需要用 10 gtts/mL 输液器在 30 分钟内输入 100 mL 生理盐水。滴速应是多少？

options.en: 10 gtts/min
options.zh: 10 gtts/min

options.en: 17 gtts/min
options.zh: 17 gtts/min

options.en: 20 gtts/min
options.zh: 20 gtts/min

options.en: 33 gtts/min
options.zh: 33 gtts/min

questions.explanationEn: 100 mL x 10 gtts/mL / 30 minutes = 1000 / 30 = approximately 33 gtts/min. Answer 17 is the error of dividing by 60 minutes; answer 20 comes from inverting the formula.
questions.explanationZh: 100 mL x 10 gtts/mL / 30 分钟 = 1000 / 30 ≈ 33 gtts/min。选 17 是错除以 60 分钟；选 20 是把公式弄反了。

questions.questionEn: When a BC protocol refers to running an IV at a maintenance rate, what flow rate does this correspond to?
questions.questionZh: 当 BC protocol 提到以 maintenance rate（维持速度）输液时，对应的流速大约是多少？

options.en: Approximately 75 mL/hr
options.zh: 大约 75 mL/hr

options.en: Approximately 150 mL/hr
options.zh: 大约 150 mL/hr

options.en: Approximately 30 mL/hr
options.zh: 大约 30 mL/hr

options.en: A wide-open line until 500 mL has infused
options.zh: 全开输注直到输完 500 mL

questions.explanationEn: The IV maintenance section states the maintenance rate is approximately 75 mL/hr, delivered through either a 10 gtts/mL macro-drip or 60 gtts/mL micro-drip set. It is distinct from a fluid bolus, which is volume-targeted (20 mL/kg) for hypoperfusion.
questions.explanationZh: IV maintenance 章节指出维持速度约为 75 mL/hr，可经 10 gtts/mL macro-drip 或 60 gtts/mL micro-drip 输液器给予。它不同于针对低灌注的 fluid bolus（按 20 mL/kg 容量目标给）。

questions.questionEn: During transport with a running IV, how often should you reassess the patient and the IV according to the maintenance guideline, and what does the check include?
questions.questionZh: 转运途中有 IV 在输注时，按 maintenance 指南应多久重新评估一次？评估包括哪些内容？

options.en: Once on arrival at hospital; check only the total volume infused
options.zh: 到医院时评估一次；只需核对总输入量

options.en: Every 30-45 minutes; check the drip chamber only
options.zh: 每 30-45 分钟一次；只检查滴壶

options.en: Every 5-15 minutes; reassess ABCs, vital signs, the IV site, tubing, solution bag, and watch for complications
options.zh: 每 5-15 分钟一次；重新评估 ABC、vitals、穿刺部位、管路和液袋，并观察并发症

options.en: Only when the pump alarms or the patient complains of pain at the site
options.zh: 只有当输液报警或病人主诉穿刺处疼痛时才评估

questions.explanationEn: IV maintenance requires regular reassessment every 5 to 15 minutes: ABCs and injury sites, vital signs, inspection of the IV site, tubing and solution bag, observation for complications, maintaining the correct flow rate, and changing the bag when required.
questions.explanationZh: IV maintenance 要求每 5-15 分钟定期重评：ABC 和损伤部位、vital signs、检查穿刺点/管路/液袋、观察并发症、维持正确滴速，并在需要时更换液袋。

questions.questionEn: Which of the following belongs on the list of critical history questions for a motor vehicle accident?
questions.questionZh: 下列哪一项属于 MVA（机动车事故）的 critical history questions 清单内容？

options.en: The patient's insurance provider and licence status
options.zh: 病人的保险公司和驾照状态

options.en: The colour and model year of the vehicles
options.zh: 车辆的颜色和出厂年份

options.en: Whether the roadway was provincially or municipally maintained
options.zh: 道路属于省道还是市政道路

options.en: Whether the vehicle had airbags and whether they deployed
options.zh: 车辆是否配有安全气囊、气囊是否弹出

questions.explanationEn: The MVA critical history list includes airbag equipment and deployment, along with impact speed, exterior and interior damage, compartment intrusion, restraint type, patient position, loss of consciousness, and the condition of other occupants including any fatality in the same vehicle.
questions.explanationZh: MVA critical history 清单包括是否配备气囊及是否弹出，以及撞击速度、车辆外部/内部损坏、车厢侵入、约束装置类型、病人初始位置、有无意识丧失、以及其他乘员情况（含同车死亡）。

questions.questionEn: A man was stabbed during an altercation outside a bar. The scene is now police-secured. Beyond the wound itself, which history details are most important to gather for the receiving trauma team?
questions.questionZh: 一名男子在酒吧外斗殴中被刺伤，警方已控制现场。除伤口本身外，为接收创伤团队收集的最重要病史细节是哪些？

options.en: The names of witnesses and the suspect's description
options.zh: 目击者姓名和嫌疑人的体貌特征

options.en: The length and width of the weapon, the number of wounds, and whether the wounds were slashed or stabbed
options.zh: 凶器的长度和宽度、伤口数量、以及伤口属于划割还是刺入

options.en: The exact time police arrived and secured the scene
options.zh: 警方到达并控制现场的确切时间

options.en: Whether the patient had consumed alcohol earlier in the evening
options.zh: 病人当晚是否饮酒

questions.explanationEn: For a stabbing, the critical history list specifies the type of weapon, its size (length and width), whether wounds are slashed or stabbed, the number of wounds, other injuries, initial position and condition, and loss of consciousness. Weapon dimensions predict depth and the cavities potentially penetrated.
questions.explanationZh: 刺伤的 critical history 清单包括凶器类型、尺寸（长度和宽度）、伤口是划割还是刺入、伤口数量、其他损伤、初始位置与状态、有无意识丧失。凶器尺寸可预测刺入深度和可能穿透的体腔。

questions.questionEn: A transfer document states the patient has been 'NPO since 0600, salbutamol prn'. Using the BC abbreviation list, this means the patient:
questions.questionZh: 转院文件写明病人「NPO since 0600, salbutamol prn」。按 BC 缩写表，这表示病人：

options.en: Has had nothing by mouth since 0600 and takes salbutamol as needed
options.zh: 从 06:00 起禁食禁水，salbutamol 按需使用

options.en: Has had no pain since 0600 and takes salbutamol nightly
options.zh: 从 06:00 起无疼痛，salbutamol 每晚使用

options.en: Received nitrous oxide at 0600 and salbutamol before meals
options.zh: 06:00 使用过氧化亚氮，salbutamol 餐前使用

options.en: Was non-palpable for pulses at 0600 and needs salbutamol immediately
options.zh: 06:00 时脉搏无法触及，需立即给 salbutamol

questions.explanationEn: NPO means nothing by mouth and prn means as needed or as required. Misreading standard abbreviations on transfer paperwork is a real safety hazard; the guideline includes the approved abbreviation list for both PCR writing and reading.
questions.explanationZh: NPO 意为禁食禁水（nothing by mouth），prn 意为按需（as needed）。误读转运文书上的标准缩写是真实的安全隐患；指南提供的缩写表既用于书写也用于阅读 PCR。

questions.questionEn: After a call involving an intoxicated patient who initially refused care, which entry is the most appropriate way to document his behaviour on the Patient Care Report?
questions.questionZh: 处理一名最初拒绝救治的醉酒病人后，在 Patient Care Report 上记录其行为的最恰当写法是哪种？

options.en: Patient was drunk and being difficult as usual for this address
options.zh: 「病人喝醉了，和这个地址一贯的情况一样难缠」

options.en: Patient appeared intoxicated; no further detail needed
options.zh: 「病人看起来醉了」——无需更多细节

options.en: Smell of alcohol on breath noted; slurred speech; patient stated 'I don't need help'; refusal discussed and patient later consented at 2145
options.zh: 「呼气有酒味；言语含糊；病人称『我不需要帮助』；已说明拒绝风险，病人于 21:45 同意接受救治」

options.en: Omit the refusal since he ultimately agreed to transport
options.zh: 既然最终同意转运，就不必记录拒绝过程

questions.explanationEn: Documentation should record objective findings (AOB, slurred speech), direct patient quotes, and times, rather than opinions or labels. The records and reports component exists to accurately capture assessment and treatment; an initial refusal and subsequent consent are clinically and legally significant events.
questions.explanationZh: 记录应写客观发现（呼气酒味 AOB、言语含糊）、病人原话引用和时间，而不是主观评价或标签。Records and reports 组件的目的就是准确记录评估与处置；先拒绝后同意在临床和法律上都是重要事件。

questions.questionEn: A 78-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes calls for 'indigestion' that started 2 hours ago. She is weak, diaphoretic, and slightly short of breath, but denies any chest pain. Her vitals: HR 96, BP 142/88, SpO2 93%. The most appropriate approach is to:
questions.questionZh: 一名 78 岁 2 型糖尿病女性因 2 小时前开始的「消化不良」呼叫救护。她乏力、出汗、轻微气促，但否认任何胸痛。Vitals：HR 96、BP 142/88、SpO2 93%。最恰当的做法是：

options.en: Treat for gastric upset and recommend she follow up with her family doctor
options.zh: 按胃部不适处理，建议她之后看家庭医生

options.en: Treat her as suspected cardiac ischemia with atypical symptoms - manage per the cardiac chest pain guideline and transport
options.zh: 按疑似心肌缺血的不典型表现处理——依 cardiac chest pain 指南处置并转运

options.en: Administer oral glucose in case this is hypoglycemia
options.zh: 先给口服葡萄糖，以防是低血糖

options.en: Ask her to walk to the stretcher to assess her exercise tolerance
options.zh: 让她走到担架旁以评估运动耐量

questions.explanationEn: Older adults, women, and diabetics frequently present with atypical ischemia: epigastric discomfort, weakness, diaphoresis, or dyspnea without chest pain. The ASA monograph explicitly covers atypical symptoms consistent with cardiac ischemia. Painless presentations are a core geriatric trap; walking the patient increases myocardial demand.
questions.explanationZh: 老年人、女性和糖尿病患者常以不典型缺血表现就诊：上腹不适、乏力、出汗或呼吸困难而无胸痛。ASA 药物专论明确将「符合心肌缺血的不典型症状」列入指征。无痛性表现是老年病学核心陷阱；让病人行走会增加心肌耗氧。

questions.questionEn: Why are elderly patients more likely than younger adults to have a myocardial infarction without chest pain?
questions.questionZh: 为什么老年病人比年轻成人更容易发生没有胸痛的心肌梗死？

options.en: Their coronary arteries are too small to generate pain signals
options.zh: 他们的冠状动脉太细，无法产生疼痛信号

options.en: They have higher pain thresholds from years of physical labour
options.zh: 多年体力劳动使他们疼痛阈值更高

options.en: Elderly hearts infarct more slowly, so pain never develops
options.zh: 老年人心肌梗死进展更慢，因此不会出现疼痛

options.en: Age-related changes and conditions such as diabetic neuropathy blunt pain perception, so ischemia may present as weakness, dyspnea, or confusion instead
options.zh: 年龄相关改变及糖尿病神经病变等使痛觉迟钝，缺血可能表现为乏力、气促或意识混乱

questions.explanationEn: Altered pain perception from aging nervous systems and comorbidities such as diabetic autonomic neuropathy means ischemia may produce weakness, syncope, dyspnea, or new confusion rather than classic crushing chest pain. This is why the guidelines recognize atypical symptoms consistent with cardiac ischemia as an ASA indication.
questions.explanationZh: 神经系统老化及糖尿病自主神经病变等共病使痛觉减退，心肌缺血可表现为乏力、晕厥、气促或新发意识混乱，而非典型压榨性胸痛。这正是指南将「符合心肌缺血的不典型症状」列为 ASA 指征的原因。

questions.questionEn: An 82-year-old man on metoprolol has had black tarry stools for two days. He is pale and diaphoretic with cool skin. His heart rate is 84. Why should the heart rate NOT reassure you?
questions.questionZh: 一名 82 岁男性服用 metoprolol（美托洛尔），黑色柏油样便两天。他面色苍白、出汗、皮肤湿冷。心率 84。为什么这个心率不能让你放心？

options.en: Beta-blockade prevents compensatory tachycardia, so he may be in significant hemorrhagic shock with a 'normal' rate
options.zh: β 受体阻滞剂抑制代偿性心动过速，他可能已处于明显失血性休克却显示「正常」心率

options.en: Elderly patients normally run heart rates over 100, so 84 is actually bradycardia requiring pacing
options.zh: 老年人正常心率应超过 100，84 其实是需要起搏的心动过缓

options.en: The heart rate is irrelevant because melena is never hemodynamically significant
options.zh: 心率无关紧要，因为黑便从不会造成血流动力学问题

options.en: Metoprolol causes false pulse oximetry readings that invalidate all vitals
options.zh: 美托洛尔会造成血氧仪读数错误，使所有 vitals 失效

questions.explanationEn: Beta-blockers cap the tachycardic response that normally signals hypovolemia, so skin signs (pale, cool, diaphoretic) become the more reliable shock indicators - and his meet the unstable criterion of cool pale clammy skin secondary to suspected shock. Treat as unstable GI hemorrhage despite the deceptively normal rate.
questions.explanationZh: β 受体阻滞剂封顶了通常提示低血容量的心率上升反应，因此皮肤征象（苍白、湿冷、出汗）成为更可靠的休克指标——他已符合「疑似休克所致湿冷苍白皮肤」这一不稳定标准。尽管心率看似正常，仍应按不稳定的消化道出血处理。

questions.questionEn: A 79-year-old woman on warfarin tripped on a rug, struck her head on the floor, and got up by herself. She has a small forehead bruise, GCS 15, and no complaints. Her son asks if she really needs to go to hospital. Your best response is based on which reasoning?
questions.questionZh: 一名服用 warfarin（华法林）的 79 岁女性被地毯绊倒，头部撞到地板，自己爬了起来。前额有小片瘀青，GCS 15，无任何主诉。她儿子问是否真的需要去医院。你的最佳回答基于哪种推理？

options.en: She can stay home because her GCS is 15 and the mechanism was minor
options.zh: GCS 15 且受伤机制轻微，可以留在家中

options.en: She only needs transport if she vomits within the next hour
options.zh: 只有当她一小时内呕吐才需要转运

options.en: Anticoagulated elderly patients can develop delayed intracranial bleeding after even minor head strikes, so transport for evaluation is warranted despite the normal exam
options.zh: 服抗凝药的老年人即使轻微头部撞击也可能发生迟发性颅内出血，因此虽然检查正常仍应转运评估

options.en: Warfarin protects against clot formation, which lowers her risk of intracranial bleeding
options.zh: 华法林抗凝反而降低了她颅内出血的风险

questions.explanationEn: Warfarin dramatically raises the risk of slow intracranial hemorrhage; age-related brain atrophy stretches bridging veins and enlarges the space in which a bleed can grow silently before signs appear. A normal initial GCS does not exclude an evolving bleed. New neurological deficits would make her definitively unstable - the goal is to be in hospital before that happens.
questions.explanationZh: 华法林显著增加缓慢性颅内出血风险；年龄相关脑萎缩牵拉桥静脉并扩大了出血可无症状积聚的空间。初始 GCS 正常不能排除进展中的出血。一旦出现新发神经功能缺损她就明确不稳定——目标是在那之前抵达医院。

questions.questionEn: An 81-year-old man fell in his kitchen. He has a painful hip and abrasions. While gathering the fall history, which question is most important for uncovering a treatable medical cause?
questions.questionZh: 一名 81 岁男性在厨房跌倒，髋部疼痛并有擦伤。采集跌倒病史时，哪个问题对发现可治疗的内科原因最重要？

options.en: What type of flooring is in the kitchen?
options.zh: 「厨房铺的是什么地板？」

options.en: What were you doing and how did you feel just before you fell - any dizziness, palpitations, or blackout?
options.zh: 「跌倒前你在做什么、有什么感觉——有没有头晕、心悸或眼前发黑？」

options.en: Have you ever fallen anywhere else in the house before?
options.zh: 「你以前在家里其他地方摔过吗？」

options.en: Do you live alone or with family?
options.zh: 「你独居还是和家人同住？」

questions.explanationEn: The critical history list for falls includes the cause of the fall. In older adults a fall is often the presenting sign of syncope, arrhythmia, hypoglycemia, stroke, or medication effect. Pre-fall symptoms distinguish a mechanical trip from a medical event that itself needs assessment and transport.
questions.explanationZh: 跌倒的 critical history 清单包含「跌倒原因」。对老年人而言，跌倒常常是晕厥、心律失常、低血糖、卒中或药物作用的首发表现。跌倒前的症状可以区分单纯绊倒和本身就需要评估转运的内科事件。

questions.questionEn: When taking a history from an elderly patient with impaired hearing, which technique is most effective?
questions.questionZh: 为听力受损的老年病人采集病史时，哪种沟通技巧最有效？

options.en: Shout loudly close to the patient's ear
options.zh: 贴近病人耳边大声喊

options.en: Direct all questions to family members to save time
options.zh: 为节省时间，把所有问题都问家属

options.en: Face the patient at eye level, speak slowly and clearly in a slightly lower pitch, and confirm understanding
options.zh: 与病人平视、面对面，放慢语速、咬字清晰、音调略低，并确认对方理解

options.en: Use only written notes and avoid speaking
options.zh: 只用写字交流，避免说话

questions.explanationEn: Age-related hearing loss affects high frequencies first, so a lower-pitched, clear, unhurried voice with the face visible (allowing lip reading) works better than shouting, which distorts speech and appears aggressive. Bypassing a competent patient for the family disrespects autonomy and loses first-hand history.
questions.explanationZh: 老年性听力下降先影响高频，因此音调略低、清晰、不急促、面部可见（便于读唇）的交流方式比喊叫更有效——喊叫会使语音失真且显得有攻击性。绕过有行为能力的病人只问家属，既不尊重其自主权也丢失了第一手病史。

questions.questionEn: Care aides report that an 86-year-old woman with dementia 'seems confused'. She is calm, answers some questions oddly, and vitals are normal. What is the single most useful piece of information to obtain next?
questions.questionZh: 护理人员报告一名 86 岁失智女性「看起来意识混乱」。她情绪平静，部分问题回答古怪，vitals 正常。接下来最有价值的信息是什么？

options.en: Her exact age and place of birth for the PCR
options.zh: 她的确切年龄和出生地，用于填写 PCR

options.en: Whether the facility has transport paperwork ready
options.zh: 机构是否已备好转运文件

options.en: Her score on a full mini mental status examination
options.zh: 完整简易精神状态检查（MMSE）的得分

options.en: Her baseline mental status from a caregiver - is today's presentation different from her normal?
options.zh: 向照护者了解她的基线精神状态——今天的表现和平时是否不同？

questions.explanationEn: In dementia, confusion alone is uninterpretable without a baseline. An acute change from baseline suggests delirium with a treatable cause - infection, hypoglycemia, hypoxia, stroke, or drug effect - and warrants full assessment including blood glucose. Chronic stable confusion is her normal. Caregivers are the essential comparator.
questions.explanationZh: 对失智病人来说，单纯「混乱」在没有基线的情况下无法解读。与基线相比的急性变化提示谵妄，背后常有可治疗原因——感染、低血糖、低氧、卒中或药物作用——需要包括血糖在内的完整评估。慢性稳定的混乱则是她的常态。照护者是必不可少的对照来源。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.57 (decreased LOC without known cause)

questions.questionEn: An 85-year-old woman with a history of recurrent UTIs has become withdrawn and confused over 24 hours. Temperature 36.4, HR 92, BP 108/64, RR 20. Her daughter says 'at least she has no fever, so it can't be an infection.' Your assessment should recognize that:
questions.questionZh: 一名有反复尿路感染史的 85 岁女性 24 小时内变得淡漠、意识混乱。体温 36.4，HR 92，BP 108/64，RR 20。女儿说「至少没发烧，所以不可能是感染」。你的评估应认识到：

options.en: Elderly patients with serious infection often fail to mount fever or marked tachycardia - new confusion may be the primary presenting sign of sepsis
options.zh: 老年人发生严重感染时常常不出现发热或明显心动过速——新发意识混乱可能就是脓毒症的主要表现

options.en: The daughter is correct - absence of fever reliably excludes infection at any age
options.zh: 女儿说得对——任何年龄无发热都能可靠排除感染

options.en: Confusion in a patient this age is always dementia and needs no acute workup
options.zh: 这个年龄的意识混乱都是失智，不需要急性期检查

options.en: A temperature of 36.4 rules out sepsis because sepsis always causes hypothermia below 35
options.zh: 36.4 的体温排除了脓毒症，因为脓毒症必然导致 35 以下的低体温

questions.explanationEn: Blunted immune and thermoregulatory responses mean older septic patients may be normothermic or hypothermic, with modest heart rates. Acute functional decline and new confusion are among the most sensitive geriatric sepsis indicators. This patient needs full assessment including blood glucose, and transport.
questions.explanationZh: 免疫与体温调节反应迟钝使老年脓毒症病人可能体温正常甚至偏低，心率变化也不明显。急性功能下降和新发意识混乱是老年脓毒症最敏感的指标之一。该病人需要包括血糖在内的完整评估并转运。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.18 (References: Nancy Caroline); p.57

questions.questionEn: Which statement best describes how normal aging changes the trauma assessment of a geriatric patient?
questions.questionZh: 关于正常衰老如何改变老年创伤评估，下列哪种说法最准确？

options.en: Aging thickens the skin, making bruising and skin tears less common
options.zh: 衰老使皮肤增厚，瘀伤和皮肤撕裂更少见

options.en: Reduced physiologic reserve means an older patient can look stable initially yet deteriorate rapidly, and lesser mechanisms can cause serious injury
options.zh: 生理储备下降意味着老年病人初期可能看似稳定却迅速恶化，较小的受伤机制也能造成严重损伤

options.en: Older bones are denser, so fractures require higher-energy mechanisms than in the young
options.zh: 老年人骨密度更高，骨折需要比年轻人更大的能量

options.en: The aging heart compensates for blood loss faster than a younger heart
options.zh: 老年心脏对失血的代偿比年轻心脏更快

questions.explanationEn: Diminished cardiac, respiratory, and renal reserve narrows the margin between compensation and collapse, while osteoporosis and fragile tissues mean low-energy mechanisms - a fall from standing - can fracture hips, ribs, or vertebrae. Maintain a lower threshold for treating geriatric trauma patients as unstable.
questions.explanationZh: 心、肺、肾储备下降使代偿与崩溃之间的余地变窄；骨质疏松和脆弱组织意味着低能量机制——如站立位跌倒——也能造成髋部、肋骨或椎体骨折。对老年创伤病人应以更低的门槛按不稳定处理。

questions.questionEn: Assessing an 88-year-old man for 'a fall', you find bruises on his forearms and back in several different stages of healing. His story of the fall keeps changing, and his adult son answers most questions for him while standing close. What is your most appropriate course of action?
questions.questionZh: 你以「跌倒」为由评估一名 88 岁男性，发现他前臂和背部有多处处于不同愈合阶段的瘀伤。他对跌倒经过的描述前后不一，而他的成年儿子紧贴在旁替他回答大多数问题。你最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Confront the son directly at the scene and demand an explanation for the bruises
options.zh: 当场质问儿子，要求解释瘀伤来源

options.en: Accept the family's explanation and document 'multiple falls' as the cause
options.zh: 接受家属解释，在记录中写「多次跌倒」作为原因

options.en: Refuse to transport until police arrive and interview the family
options.zh: 在警方到场并询问家属之前拒绝转运

options.en: Try to assess and speak with the patient privately, document all findings and statements objectively, transport, and report your concerns through the appropriate channel
options.zh: 设法与病人单独交流评估，客观记录所有发现和陈述，转运病人，并按规定渠道上报你的疑虑

questions.explanationEn: Bruises in multiple healing stages, inconsistent history, and a controlling caregiver are recognized elder abuse indicators. The paramedic's role is objective documentation - locations, sizes, colours, direct quotes - separating the patient for private conversation when possible, transporting, and reporting concerns; not scene confrontation or accusation, which can escalate danger for the patient.
questions.explanationZh: 多阶段愈合的瘀伤、前后矛盾的病史和控制性照护者是公认的老年虐待警示信号。救护员的职责是客观记录——部位、大小、颜色、原话引用——尽量创造与病人单独交流的机会、转运并上报疑虑；而不是现场对质或指控，那可能加剧病人的危险。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.10, p.18 (References: Nancy Caroline)

questions.questionEn: An 88-year-old woman with known osteoporosis slipped from a low step and landed on her buttocks. She has midline mid-back pain but can move all limbs, with normal vitals. Which reasoning should guide your management?
questions.questionZh: 一名已知骨质疏松的 88 岁女性从矮台阶滑落坐倒在地。她主诉背部中线中段疼痛，但四肢活动正常，vitals 正常。哪种推理应指导你的处置？

options.en: A fall from a low step cannot generate enough force to fracture the spine, so no precautions are needed
options.zh: 矮台阶跌倒的能量不足以造成脊柱骨折，无需任何保护措施

options.en: Since she can move all four limbs, a spinal fracture is excluded
options.zh: 四肢都能活动，说明脊柱骨折已被排除

options.en: Osteoporotic bone can fracture with minimal force - midline back pain after even a low fall warrants spinal assessment and precautions
options.zh: 骨质疏松的骨骼受很小外力也会骨折——即使低处跌倒，出现背部中线疼痛也应做脊柱评估和保护

options.en: Give analgesia and leave her at home with instructions to rest in bed for a week
options.zh: 给予镇痛后让她留在家中卧床休息一周

questions.explanationEn: Osteoporosis rewrites the usual relationship between mechanism and injury: vertebral compression fractures commonly follow trivial falls. Midline pain is a NEXUS-relevant finding, and intact limb movement does not exclude an unstable fracture. Assess, apply spinal motion restriction as indicated, and transport.
questions.explanationZh: 骨质疏松改写了机制与损伤之间的常规对应关系：椎体压缩骨折常发生于很轻微的跌倒之后。中线压痛是 NEXUS 相关阳性发现，四肢活动正常并不能排除不稳定骨折。应评估、按指征实施脊柱活动限制并转运。

questions.questionEn: When transporting an elderly patient who takes multiple medications, why is bringing the complete, current medication list (or the actual bottles) to hospital a priority?
questions.questionZh: 转运服用多种药物的老年病人时，为什么把完整、最新的用药清单（或药瓶本身）带到医院是优先事项？

options.en: Polypharmacy causes interactions and adverse effects that may explain the presentation, and the list guides both prehospital decisions and hospital care
options.zh: 多重用药造成的相互作用和不良反应可能正是发病原因，清单同时指导院前决策和院内治疗

options.en: It is only needed for billing purposes at the receiving facility
options.zh: 只是接收医院计费需要

options.en: Medications are irrelevant to assessment once the patient is symptomatic
options.zh: 病人一旦出现症状，用药情况就与评估无关了

options.en: The list only matters if the patient is unconscious
options.zh: 只有病人昏迷时清单才重要

questions.explanationEn: Drug effects and interactions - beta-blockers masking tachycardia, anticoagulants raising bleed risk, sedatives causing falls, diuretics causing electrolyte loss - are frequent causes or modifiers of geriatric emergencies. The medication history also feeds directly into protocol contraindication checks such as those for ASA and nitroglycerin.
questions.explanationZh: 药物作用与相互作用——β 阻滞剂掩盖心动过速、抗凝药增加出血风险、镇静剂导致跌倒、利尿剂造成电解质丢失——是老年急症的常见原因或修饰因素。用药史还直接用于 ASA、硝酸甘油等 protocol 的禁忌症核查。

questions.questionEn: You find a 77-year-old man on his bathroom floor. He does not respond to loud verbal commands, but groans and pushes your hand away when you apply a trapezius squeeze. On AVPU he is rated:
questions.questionZh: 你在卫生间地板上发现一名 77 岁男性。他对大声呼唤没有反应，但斜方肌掐捏时会呻吟并推开你的手。按 AVPU 他应评为：

options.en: A, because pushing your hand away is purposeful movement
options.zh: A——因为推开你的手属于有目的的动作

options.en: V, because he made a sound
options.zh: V——因为他发出了声音

options.en: U, because he cannot follow commands
options.zh: U——因为他不能遵嘱动作

options.en: P - he responds only to pain; monitor the airway closely and place him semi-prone if injuries permit
options.zh: P——只对疼痛刺激有反应；需严密监测气道，如损伤允许应置于 semi-prone 体位

questions.explanationEn: Response only to painful stimulus is P on AVPU. The guideline instructs close airway monitoring with intervention as necessary, and semi-prone positioning if injuries permit, because a patient at P cannot reliably protect the airway. Groaning triggered by pain is not a verbal response to voice.
questions.explanationZh: 只对疼痛刺激有反应在 AVPU 中评为 P。指南要求严密监测气道并按需干预，如损伤允许摆 semi-prone 体位，因为 P 级病人无法可靠保护气道。疼痛引发的呻吟不属于对言语的反应。

questions.questionEn: An 80-year-old woman fell against a coffee table. She is alert with a bleeding laceration above her right eyebrow and neck stiffness. Which primary survey intervention indication applies?
questions.questionZh: 一名 80 岁女性跌倒撞到茶几。她神志清楚，右眉上方有出血性裂伤，并有颈部僵硬感。适用哪一条 primary survey 干预指征？

options.en: Cervical spine stabilization - she has an obvious injury above the level of the clavicles
options.zh: 颈椎固定——她有锁骨水平以上的明显损伤

options.en: Obstructed airway procedures - facial wounds always compromise the airway
options.zh: 气道梗阻处理——面部伤口必然影响气道

options.en: No intervention - alert patients never need spinal precautions
options.zh: 无需干预——清醒病人从不需要脊柱保护

options.en: Rapid cooling - to reduce swelling around the laceration
options.zh: 快速降温——以减少裂伤周围肿胀

questions.explanationEn: Obvious injury above the level of the clavicles is a listed indication for cervical spine stabilization, and her neck symptoms reinforce it. Age and osteoporosis raise the risk that even this modest mechanism injured the cervical spine. The laceration is controlled with direct pressure during the survey.
questions.explanationZh: 锁骨水平以上的明显损伤是颈椎固定的明确指征之一，她的颈部症状进一步支持。年龄和骨质疏松使这种不大的机制也可能伤及颈椎。裂伤在检查过程中以直接压迫控制。

questions.questionEn: A 90-year-old man with severe kyphosis requires spinal motion restriction after a fall down three stairs. When you lay him on the board his head hovers well above the surface and he cannot straighten. You should:
questions.questionZh: 一名严重驼背（kyphosis）的 90 岁男性从三级台阶跌落后需要脊柱活动限制。放到板上时他的头部悬空远离板面，无法伸直。你应该：

options.en: Firmly press the head down to the board and secure it with tape
options.zh: 用力将头压到板面并用胶带固定

options.en: Pad generously under the head and shoulders to support his habitual curvature and immobilize him in his own neutral position
options.zh: 在头和肩下充分垫衬，支撑他习惯的脊柱曲度，在其自身的中立位上固定

options.en: Skip immobilization entirely because it is impossible in kyphotic patients
options.zh: 驼背病人无法固定，干脆完全放弃固定

options.en: Transport him prone so the curvature faces upward
options.zh: 让他俯卧转运，使弯曲的背部朝上

questions.explanationEn: Immobilization means securing the spine in the patient's own neutral alignment, not an idealized flat position. Forcing a rigidly kyphotic spine straight can cause fractures and pain. Filling the voids with padding achieves motion restriction while respecting fixed deformity. Note the guideline also cautions against taping the head as the sole securing method.
questions.explanationZh: 固定的含义是在病人自身的中立对线上限制脊柱活动，而不是强求理想化的平躺位。强行压直僵硬驼背的脊柱可造成骨折和剧痛。用垫料填满空隙既能限制活动又尊重固定畸形。另注意指南提醒不要用胶带固定头部作为唯一手段。

questions.questionEn: A 76-year-old woman with CHF is in respiratory distress, sitting bolt upright at 0300, SpO2 88%. During the primary survey, which combination of survey interventions is indicated?
questions.questionZh: 一名 76 岁 CHF 女性凌晨 3 点端坐呼吸窘迫，SpO2 88%。Primary survey 中应采取哪组 survey interventions？

options.en: Lay her flat and apply a blanket for warmth
options.zh: 让她平躺并盖毯保暖

options.en: Withhold oxygen until a full set of vitals is documented
options.zh: 在记录完整 vitals 之前暂不给氧

options.en: Oxygen for respiratory distress, keep her positioned upright with legs down, keep her at rest and warm
options.zh: 因呼吸窘迫给氧，保持她直立坐位、双腿下垂，保持静息并注意保暖

options.en: Position her semi-prone to protect the airway
options.zh: 置于 semi-prone 体位以保护气道

questions.explanationEn: Oxygen is a primary survey intervention indicated by respiratory distress, and position is another listed survey intervention - for CHF/pulmonary edema the guideline specifies sitting upright with legs hung down, at rest, kept warm. Laying her flat would worsen pulmonary edema; oxygen is never delayed for paperwork.
questions.explanationZh: 给氧是 primary survey 干预之一，指征包括呼吸窘迫；体位（Position）也是列明的 survey intervention——对 CHF/肺水肿，指南指定直立坐位、双腿下垂、静息、保暖。让她平躺会加重肺水肿；给氧绝不能为记录 vitals 而延迟。

questions.questionEn: You have completed the primary survey of a stable 74-year-old man with abdominal pain and decided he does not require immediate transport. According to the assessment model, the secondary survey you now begin consists of:
questions.questionZh: 你已完成一名腹痛、情况稳定的 74 岁男性的 primary survey，判断暂不需要立即转运。按评估模型，你接下来开始的 secondary survey 包括：

options.en: History, vital signs, head-to-toe examination, and functional inquiry
options.zh: History、vital signs、head-to-toe examination，以及 functional inquiry

options.en: Rapid body survey, transport decision, and protocols
options.zh: Rapid body survey、transport decision 和 protocols

options.en: Hazards, environment, mechanism, people, and resources
options.zh: Hazards、environment、mechanism、people 和 resources

options.en: Hand-off report and documentation
options.zh: Hand-off report 和 documentation

questions.explanationEn: The secondary survey comprises history, vital signs, head-to-toe examination, and (PCP required) functional inquiry. Its purpose is to identify the chief complaint, establish baseline vitals, and gather information about the condition. Option B mixes primary survey steps; C is the RSE; D is records and reports.
questions.explanationZh: Secondary survey 由 history、vital signs、head-to-toe examination 和（PCP 必做的）functional inquiry 组成，目的是明确 chief complaint、建立基线 vitals 并收集病情信息。选项 B 混入了 primary survey 步骤；C 是 RSE；D 是 records and reports。

questions.questionEn: A talkative 83-year-old woman called for her chronic knee pain, but as you assess her you notice she is speaking in shorter sentences than when you arrived and her breathing has become laboured with accessory muscle use. She insists she just wants to discuss her knee. You should:
questions.questionZh: 一名健谈的 83 岁女性因慢性膝痛呼叫救护，但评估过程中你注意到她说话的句子比你刚到时明显变短，呼吸变得费力并出现辅助呼吸肌使用。她坚持只想谈膝盖的问题。你应该：

options.en: Complete the knee assessment first since it is her stated chief complaint
options.zh: 先完成膝部评估，因为那是她自述的 chief complaint

options.en: Document the breathing change and continue the interview as planned
options.zh: 记录呼吸变化，按原计划继续问诊

options.en: Advise her to book a family doctor appointment for the breathing
options.zh: 建议她为呼吸问题预约家庭医生

options.en: Return to the primary survey - new respiratory distress is an unstable finding that takes priority over the chronic complaint
options.zh: 回到 primary survey——新出现的呼吸窘迫属于不稳定表现，优先级高于慢性主诉

questions.explanationEn: Assessment is dynamic: whenever a life-threat emerges, the paramedic returns to the primary survey. Respiratory distress with accessory muscle use is an unstable criterion requiring oxygen and a transport decision. Elderly patients frequently minimize or misattribute serious symptoms; the crew's observations outrank the stated agenda.
questions.explanationZh: 评估是动态的：一旦出现威胁生命的问题，就应回到 primary survey。呼吸窘迫伴辅助呼吸肌使用属于不稳定标准，需要给氧并做转运决策。老年病人经常淡化或错误归因严重症状；救护员的客观观察优先于病人自述的议题。

questions.questionEn: A 72-year-old man with a previous hip replacement felt his hip 'pop out' while bending; his leg is now shortened and internally rotated. Distal pulses are present. What does the BC guideline say about his transport category?
questions.questionZh: 一名做过髋关节置换的 72 岁男性弯腰时感到髋部「弹出」；患腿现在缩短并内旋，远端脉搏存在。BC 指南对他的转运分类怎么规定？

options.en: All hip dislocations are in the Rapid Transport Category
options.zh: 所有髋关节脱位都属于 Rapid Transport Category

options.en: Hip dislocations are rapid transport only when distal pulses are absent
options.zh: 只有远端脉搏消失的髋脱位才需要快速转运

options.en: Prosthetic hip dislocations are excluded from rapid transport rules
options.zh: 人工髋关节脱位不适用快速转运规则

options.en: He may wait for a scheduled transfer since this is a recurrent problem
options.zh: 这属于复发问题，可以等待预约转院

questions.explanationEn: The guideline states plainly: all hip dislocations are in the Rapid Transport Category, because early medical reduction is essential to avoid serious long-term complications. (Isolated hip fractures, by contrast, become rapid transport when there is neurovascular impairment.) Support the limb, secure to the stretcher, and monitor distal pulses en route.
questions.explanationZh: 指南明确写道：所有髋关节脱位都属于 Rapid Transport Category，因为早期医疗复位对避免严重长期并发症至关重要。（相比之下，孤立髋部骨折在有神经血管损害时才升为快速转运。）应支撑患肢、固定于担架，途中监测远端脉搏。

questions.questionEn: An 85-year-old woman fell and has an isolated suspected hip fracture: shortened, externally rotated left leg. Her left foot is cold and you cannot palpate the pedal pulse. This finding changes her management because:
questions.questionZh: 一名 85 岁女性跌倒后疑似孤立性髋部骨折：左腿缩短外旋。她的左脚发凉，足背动脉无法触及。这个发现改变她的处置，因为：

options.en: A cold foot is normal in the elderly and requires no change
options.zh: 老年人脚凉很正常，无需改变处置

options.en: She now needs a traction splint applied to the hip
options.zh: 她现在需要对髋部使用牵引夹板

options.en: An isolated hip fracture with neurovascular impairment becomes a rapid transport patient
options.zh: 伴神经血管损害的孤立髋部骨折升级为快速转运病人

options.en: The absent pulse only matters if the skin is also mottled
options.zh: 只有皮肤同时出现花斑，脉搏消失才有意义

questions.explanationEn: Isolated hip fractures are rapid transport if there is neuro or vascular impairment - a cold, pulseless foot is exactly that. Traction splints are indicated for mid-shaft femur fractures, not hip fractures. Quickly support the limb, secure her to a firm stretcher, and transport rapidly with frequent distal checks.
questions.explanationZh: 孤立髋部骨折在存在神经或血管损害时即为快速转运——脚凉、无脉正是血管损害。牵引夹板的指征是股骨中段骨折，不是髋部骨折。应迅速支撑患肢、固定于硬担架，快速转运并频繁复查远端循环。

questions.questionEn: A 77-year-old man slipped from a standing position in his garage. On assessment his speech is newly slurred and his left hand grip is weaker than the right - his wife confirms both are new since the fall. Vitals are normal. Although the mechanism seems minor, he is categorized as:
questions.questionZh: 一名 77 岁男性在车库里从站立位滑倒。评估时发现他言语含糊是新出现的，左手握力比右手弱——妻子确认这两项都是跌倒后才有的。Vitals 正常。尽管机制看似轻微，他应被归类为：

options.en: Stable, because a fall from standing height never meets mechanism criteria
options.zh: 稳定——因为站立高度跌倒从不满足机制标准

options.en: Unstable - new onset neurological deficits are an anatomical criterion regardless of mechanism, and a stroke may have caused the fall
options.zh: 不稳定——新发神经功能缺损是解剖学标准，与机制无关；而且卒中可能正是跌倒的原因

options.en: Stable, provided his blood pressure stays under 180 systolic
options.zh: 稳定——只要收缩压保持在 180 以下

options.en: Unstable only if his GCS drops below 13
options.zh: 只有 GCS 降到 13 以下才算不稳定

questions.explanationEn: New onset neurological deficits sit on the anatomical instability list, and suspected CVA is a primary survey instability criterion - both independent of mechanism. In the elderly, always ask whether a medical event caused the fall: slurred speech plus unilateral weakness demands FAST-VAN evaluation, timely transport, and early notification.
questions.explanationZh: 新发神经功能缺损位列解剖学不稳定标准，疑似 CVA 也是 primary survey 不稳定标准——两者都与机制无关。对老年人要始终追问是否内科事件导致了跌倒：言语含糊加单侧无力需要 FAST-VAN 评估、及时转运并提前通知医院。

questions.questionEn: A care home reports an 84-year-old woman with a sudden facial droop and arm drift noticed 40 minutes ago. Under the BC instability criteria, a suspected CVA is:
questions.questionZh: 养老院报告一名 84 岁女性 40 分钟前突然出现口角歪斜和手臂下垂。按 BC 不稳定标准，疑似 CVA（脑血管意外）属于：

options.en: A stable condition if the patient can still swallow
options.zh: 只要病人还能吞咽就属于稳定

options.en: Unstable only when accompanied by unconsciousness
options.zh: 只有伴意识丧失时才不稳定

options.en: A condition to monitor at the facility for progression over 2 hours
options.zh: 应在机构内观察 2 小时看是否进展

options.en: A listed unstable primary survey finding - recognize with FAST-VAN, transport in a timely manner, and notify the receiving facility en route
options.zh: 明确列入 primary survey 不稳定标准——用 FAST-VAN 识别、及时转运并在途中通知接收医院

questions.explanationEn: Suspected CVA appears on the unstable findings list, and the stroke guideline requires accurate recognition (FAST-VAN), timely transport, and en-route notification, because time determines eligibility for reperfusion therapy. Waiting to see if deficits resolve wastes the treatment window.
questions.explanationZh: 疑似 CVA 在不稳定表现清单中，stroke 指南要求准确识别（FAST-VAN）、及时转运并途中通知医院，因为时间窗决定再灌注治疗资格。留观等待缺损是否消退会浪费治疗窗口。

questions.questionEn: An 84-year-old man has vomited dark blood twice. He is anxious, with cool, pale, clammy skin. Based on the primary survey findings alone, he is:
questions.questionZh: 一名 84 岁男性两次呕吐深色血液。他焦虑不安，皮肤湿冷苍白。仅根据 primary survey 发现，他属于：

options.en: Unstable - cool pale clammy skin secondary to suspected shock is a listed criterion; position supine, keep warm, give oxygen, and transport rapidly
options.zh: 不稳定——疑似休克所致的湿冷苍白皮肤是明确标准；应平卧、保暖、给氧并快速转运

options.en: Stable until his systolic blood pressure is confirmed below 90
options.zh: 在确认收缩压低于 90 之前都算稳定

options.en: Stable because hematemesis is usually self-limiting
options.zh: 稳定——因为呕血通常会自限

options.en: Unstable only if he vomits a third time during your assessment
options.zh: 只有评估期间第三次呕血才算不稳定

questions.explanationEn: Cool pale clammy skin secondary to suspected shock is itself an unstable primary survey finding - no confirmatory BP threshold is required before acting. Hypovolemia management applies: supine positioning, warmth, supplemental oxygen to SpO2 of at least 94%, and rapid transport, with airway vigilance given ongoing vomiting.
questions.explanationZh: 疑似休克所致的湿冷苍白皮肤本身就是 primary survey 不稳定表现——不需要等血压数值确认再行动。按 hypovolemia 处理：平卧、保暖、给氧维持 SpO2 ≥ 94%、快速转运，并因持续呕吐保持气道警惕。

questions.questionEn: An 87-year-old woman with moderate dementia is assessed after a fall. Her eyes are open spontaneously, she speaks in sentences but is disoriented to place and date, and she follows simple commands. Her GCS is:
questions.questionZh: 一名中度失智的 87 岁女性跌倒后接受评估。她自发睁眼，能成句说话但对地点和日期定向障碍，可以完成简单指令。她的 GCS 是：

options.en: GCS 15, because dementia does not affect scoring
options.zh: GCS 15——因为失智不影响评分

options.en: GCS 12
options.zh: GCS 12

options.en: GCS 14 (E4 V4 M6) - and it must be interpreted against her known baseline
options.zh: GCS 14（E4 V4 M6）——且必须对照她已知的基线来解读

options.en: GCS cannot be scored in patients with dementia
options.zh: 失智病人无法进行 GCS 评分

questions.explanationEn: Spontaneous eye opening is E4, confused conversation is V4, obeying commands is M6: GCS 14. In dementia the raw score must be compared with baseline: if she is always disoriented, 14 may be her normal; if she was oriented yesterday, the same 14 is an acute change demanding urgent evaluation. Document both the score and the baseline source.
questions.explanationZh: 自发睁眼 E4，混乱对话 V4，遵嘱动作 M6：GCS 14。对失智病人，分数必须对照基线解读：如果她平时就定向障碍，14 可能是常态；如果她昨天还定向正常，同样的 14 就是需要紧急评估的急性变化。应同时记录分数和基线信息来源。

questions.questionEn: A 79-year-old man fell down a flight of stairs. He opens his eyes when you speak loudly, utters random inappropriate words, and localizes to a painful stimulus. What is his GCS and TBI classification?
questions.questionZh: 一名 79 岁男性从整段楼梯摔下。大声呼唤时他会睁眼，说出零散且不恰当的词语，对疼痛刺激能定位。他的 GCS 和 TBI 分级是什么？

options.en: GCS 13 - mild traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 13 —— 轻度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: GCS 11 (E3 V3 M5) - moderate traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 11（E3 V3 M5）—— 中度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: GCS 9 - moderate traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 9 —— 中度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: GCS 8 - severe traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 8 —— 重度创伤性脑损伤

questions.explanationEn: Eye opening to voice is E3, inappropriate words V3, localizing to pain M5: total 11, in the moderate band (9-12). Management includes oxygenation to SpO2 of at least 94%, head elevated 30 degrees, and for PCP maintaining systolic BP above 120 mmHg. In an anticoagulated elderly faller, expect deterioration and reassess frequently.
questions.explanationZh: 呼唤睁眼 E3，不恰当词语 V3，疼痛定位 M5：合计 11，属中度（9-12）。处理包括维持 SpO2 ≥ 94%、床头抬高 30 度，PCP 需维持收缩压 > 120 mmHg。对服抗凝药的老年跌倒者要预期恶化并频繁复评。

questions.questionEn: A 76-year-old woman with long-standing hypertension (usual BP around 165/95 per her home log) has vomited coffee-ground material. She is pale with HR 104. Her BP reads 118/76. How should you interpret this blood pressure?
questions.questionZh: 一名长期高血压的 76 岁女性（家庭记录平时血压约 165/95）呕吐咖啡渣样物。她面色苍白，HR 104。现测血压 118/76。你应如何解读这个血压？

options.en: It is a textbook-normal reading, so her volume status is adequate
options.zh: 这是教科书上的正常血压，说明容量状态良好

options.en: It proves her home log was inaccurate
options.zh: 这证明她的家庭血压记录不准确

options.en: It should be ignored because automated cuffs fail in the elderly
options.zh: 应忽略此读数，因为电子血压计对老年人不准

options.en: For a chronic hypertensive this represents a marked drop from baseline - treat it as relative hypotension with significant volume loss
options.zh: 对慢性高血压病人来说，这相比基线是明显下降——应视为伴显著容量丢失的相对性低血压

questions.explanationEn: A 'normal' number can hide a 45-plus mmHg fall from an elderly hypertensive's baseline - a large perfusion deficit, corroborated here by pallor and tachycardia. Geriatric vitals must be read against the individual baseline, not population norms. Manage as hypovolemia from GI bleeding: supine, warm, oxygen, rapid transport, and PCP vascular access en route.
questions.explanationZh: 「正常」数值可能掩盖了比老年高血压病人基线低了 45 mmHg 以上的下降——这是很大的灌注缺口，且已有苍白和心动过速佐证。老年 vitals 必须对照个体基线而非人群标准解读。按消化道出血所致 hypovolemia 处理：平卧、保暖、给氧、快速转运，PCP 途中建立静脉通路。

questions.questionEn: An elderly patient reports feeling faint each time she stands up after starting a new diuretic. Which vital signs approach best evaluates this complaint?
questions.questionZh: 一名老年病人报告开始服用新的利尿剂后每次站起都感到快要晕倒。哪种 vitals 评估方式最适合评估这一主诉？

options.en: Compare lying and standing readings - a marked heart rate rise or systolic drop with symptoms on standing suggests volume depletion
options.zh: 对比卧位和站立位读数——站立时心率明显上升或收缩压明显下降并伴症状，提示容量不足

options.en: Take a single seated blood pressure, which reflects all positions
options.zh: 只测一次坐位血压，它能代表所有体位

options.en: Measure blood pressure in both arms simultaneously
options.zh: 同时测量双上肢血压

options.en: Check only the oxygen saturation since dizziness is a hypoxia symptom
options.zh: 只查血氧饱和度，因为头晕是缺氧症状

questions.explanationEn: Positional (orthostatic) assessment compares supine and standing vitals: a significant HR increase or SBP fall with symptom reproduction points to volume depletion - common with diuretics in the elderly, whose blunted baroreceptor reflexes compensate poorly. Perform it only when the patient is otherwise safe to stand, with the crew guarding against a fall.
questions.explanationZh: 体位性（orthostatic）评估对比卧位与站立位 vitals：心率明显上升或收缩压下降并复现症状，提示容量不足——在服用利尿剂、压力感受器反射迟钝的老年人中很常见。只有病人可以安全站立时才做该检查，且救护员应在旁防跌倒。

questions.questionEn: A 90-year-old man fainted at lunch. He takes metoprolol and digoxin. Now: HR 40 and regular, BP 88/54, he is pale and lightheaded. The most accurate clinical interpretation is:
questions.questionZh: 一名 90 岁男性午餐时晕厥。他服用 metoprolol 和 digoxin。现在：HR 40 且规则，BP 88/54，面色苍白、头晕。最准确的临床解读是：

options.en: A heart rate of 40 is acceptable in the very old and needs no action
options.zh: 高龄老人心率 40 可以接受，无需处理

options.en: His bradycardia is compensatory and protective, so transport is optional
options.zh: 他的心动过缓是保护性代偿，可以不转运

options.en: Symptomatic bradycardia with hypotension - likely contributed to by his rate-controlling medications - makes him unstable; give oxygen, keep him supine, and transport promptly with the medication list
options.zh: 症状性心动过缓伴低血压——很可能与他的控率药物有关——属于不稳定；应给氧、平卧、尽快转运并携带用药清单

options.en: The digoxin proves this is an overdose requiring immediate naloxone
options.zh: 服用 digoxin 说明这是需要立即给 naloxone 的药物过量

questions.explanationEn: Syncope, HR 40, and BP 88/54 together mean hypoperfusion - a symptomatic bradycardia, plausibly worsened by beta-blockade and digoxin. He is unstable and needs oxygen, supine positioning, prompt transport, and the medication list for the receiving team. Naloxone reverses opioids, not cardiac glycosides.
questions.explanationZh: 晕厥、HR 40、BP 88/54 合起来就是灌注不足——症状性心动过缓，很可能被 β 阻滞剂和 digoxin 加重。他属于不稳定，需要给氧、平卧、尽快转运，并把用药清单交给接收团队。Naloxone 逆转的是阿片类，不是强心苷。

questions.questionEn: You are transporting an 81-year-old woman on apixaban who struck her head. Her GCS was 15 on scene; 20 minutes into transport she is drowsy, opening eyes to voice and now confused - GCS 13. The most appropriate response is to:
questions.questionZh: 你正在转运一名服用 apixaban（阿哌沙班）、头部受伤的 81 岁女性。现场 GCS 15；转运 20 分钟后她变得嗜睡，呼唤才睁眼且出现意识混乱——GCS 13。最恰当的反应是：

options.en: Let her sleep - drowsiness is expected after a stressful event
options.zh: 让她睡——应激事件后嗜睡是正常的

options.en: Recognize a falling GCS in an anticoagulated head injury as probable intracranial bleeding: reassess ABCs, support oxygenation to at least 94%, elevate the head 30 degrees, and notify the receiving facility
options.zh: 把服抗凝药的头伤病人 GCS 下降识别为很可能的颅内出血：重评 ABC、维持 SpO2 ≥ 94%、床头抬高 30 度并通知接收医院

options.en: Record the new score and continue without other changes since 13 is still 'mild'
options.zh: 记录新分数即可，13 仍属「轻度」，无需其他改变

options.en: Administer oral glucose in case of hypoglycemia before doing anything else
options.zh: 先给口服葡萄糖以防低血糖，再做其他处理

questions.explanationEn: The direction of change matters more than the absolute number: a two-point fall in an anticoagulated elderly head injury signals an evolving bleed. TBI care applies - oxygenation at 94% or above, head of bed at 30 degrees, loosened collar - plus early notification. A drowsy patient with a compromised airway risk should never simply be left to sleep; oral glucose requires an intact airway and a confirmed low glucose.
questions.explanationZh: 变化的方向比绝对值更重要：服抗凝药的老年头伤病人 GCS 下降 2 分提示出血正在进展。按 TBI 处理——SpO2 ≥ 94%、床头 30 度、松开颈托——并尽早通知医院。嗜睡且有气道风险的病人绝不能放任入睡；口服葡萄糖需要气道完好且确认血糖低才能给。

questions.questionEn: A 92-year-old woman with advanced dementia and a suspected femur fracture cannot answer the 0-10 pain scale. She is grimacing, guarding the leg, breathing at 28, and became agitated when moved. How should you assess and treat her pain?
questions.questionZh: 一名晚期失智的 92 岁女性疑似股骨骨折，无法回答 0-10 疼痛评分。她表情痛苦、护住患腿、呼吸 28 次/分，搬动时变得躁动。你应如何评估和处理她的疼痛？

options.en: Record 'pain assessment impossible' and withhold analgesia
options.zh: 记录「无法评估疼痛」并不给镇痛

options.en: Assume dementia patients feel less pain and treat only if she cries out
options.zh: 假定失智病人痛觉减退，只有她喊叫才处理

options.en: Ask her repeatedly until she produces a number for the scale
options.zh: 反复追问直到她说出一个疼痛数字

options.en: Use behavioural and physiological indicators - grimacing, guarding, agitation on movement, elevated respiratory rate - as evidence of significant pain and manage it before movement per the protocol
options.zh: 把行为和生理指标——表情痛苦、护腿、搬动时躁动、呼吸增快——作为明显疼痛的证据，并按 protocol 在搬动前给予镇痛

questions.explanationEn: Dementia impairs pain reporting, not pain perception. Behavioural cues (grimacing, guarding, agitation with movement) and physiological signs substitute for the numeric scale. The musculoskeletal guideline calls for analgesia prior to movement in appropriate patients - untreated pain in dementia frequently presents as 'agitation' and then gets mislabelled.
questions.explanationZh: 失智损害的是疼痛的表达，不是疼痛的感受。行为线索（表情痛苦、护腿、搬动时躁动）和生理征象可替代数字评分。骨骼肌肉损伤指南要求对合适的病人在搬动前给予镇痛——失智病人未处理的疼痛常表现为「躁动」而被误判。

questions.questionEn: A neighbour found an 86-year-old man on his kitchen floor; nobody knows how long he was down. For the spinal management decision specifically, which critical history question matters most?
questions.questionZh: 邻居发现一名 86 岁男性倒在厨房地板上，没人知道他倒了多久。就脊柱处置决策而言，哪个 critical history 问题最重要？

options.en: Has he moved himself or been moved by anyone since the fall?
options.zh: 「跌倒后他自己动过吗？有人搬动过他吗？」

options.en: What did he eat for his last meal?
options.zh: 「他最后一餐吃了什么？」

options.en: Does he have a family doctor in the area?
options.zh: 「他在本地有家庭医生吗？」

options.en: How often does the neighbour check on him?
options.zh: 「邻居多久来看他一次？」

questions.explanationEn: The fall history list includes 'has the patient moved or been moved since the incident' - it shapes spinal assessment (movement without symptoms is informative; well-meaning bystander movement may have worsened an injury) and documentation. Height, landing surface, first point of impact, LOC, and cause of fall complete the picture, alongside downtime concerns such as hypothermia and pressure injury.
questions.explanationZh: 跌倒 critical history 清单中包括「事发后病人是否自行移动或被移动过」——它直接影响脊柱评估（活动后无症状有参考意义；好心旁人的搬动可能加重损伤）和记录。坠落高度、落地面、先着地部位、有无意识丧失和跌倒原因补全信息，同时还要关注长时间倒地的低体温和压疮问题。

questions.questionEn: A 79-year-old man drove his car slowly into a light pole. Damage is minor and he is uninjured but seems vague about what happened. Which line of history questioning adds the most clinical value?
questions.questionZh: 一名 79 岁男性驾车低速撞上灯柱。车损轻微，他没有受伤，但对事发经过表述含糊。哪条病史追问最有临床价值？

options.en: Whether his insurance covers single-vehicle collisions
options.zh: 他的保险是否涵盖单车事故

options.en: How long he has owned the vehicle
options.zh: 这辆车他开了多少年

options.en: What he experienced immediately before impact - chest pain, palpitations, dizziness, confusion, or loss of consciousness
options.zh: 撞击前一刻他有什么感觉——胸痛、心悸、头晕、意识混乱或意识丧失

options.en: Whether the pole belongs to the city or a private lot
options.zh: 灯柱属于市政还是私人停车场

questions.explanationEn: The MVA history list includes loss of consciousness and the events of the crash. In older drivers, a low-speed single-vehicle impact is a classic footprint of a medical event behind the wheel - arrhythmia, TIA, hypoglycemia, or syncope. Vagueness about the moment of impact strengthens that suspicion, and the medical cause matters more than the minor trauma.
questions.explanationZh: MVA 病史清单包含意识丧失和事故经过。对高龄驾驶者，低速单车撞击是驾驶中发生内科事件的经典痕迹——心律失常、TIA、低血糖或晕厥。对撞击瞬间的含糊描述会加重这种怀疑，内科原因比轻微外伤更重要。

questions.questionEn: You transport an 88-year-old woman with dementia whose history came mostly from her daughter. Which PCR documentation practice is most appropriate?
questions.questionZh: 你转运一名 88 岁失智女性，病史主要由女儿提供。哪种 PCR 记录方式最恰当？

options.en: Write the history as if the patient provided it, to keep the narrative simple
options.zh: 把病史写成病人自己提供的，让叙述简洁一些

options.en: Record the history source ('history per daughter'), the patient's stated baseline mental status, and today's objective findings for comparison
options.zh: 注明病史来源（「病史由女儿提供」）、家属描述的基线精神状态，以及今天的客观发现以供对比

options.en: Omit the mental status section because dementia makes it meaningless
options.zh: 省略精神状态部分——失智让它失去意义

options.en: Document only vital signs since the history is second-hand
options.zh: 既然病史是二手的，只记录 vitals 即可

questions.explanationEn: Accurate records identify the information source and preserve the baseline-versus-today comparison, which is the key diagnostic axis in dementia patients. The receiving team's ability to judge 'acute change' depends entirely on what you capture at the scene - the daughter may not accompany the patient.
questions.explanationZh: 准确的记录应注明信息来源，并保留「基线 vs 今天」的对比——这是失智病人最关键的诊断轴线。接收团队判断「急性变化」的能力完全取决于你在现场记下的内容——女儿未必会陪同到院。

questions.questionEn: For a frail 84-year-old transfer patient you are asked to run the IV at the standard maintenance rate of 75 mL/hr using a micro-drip set (60 gtts/mL). What drip rate is that?
questions.questionZh: 为一名体弱的 84 岁转院病人，需要用 micro-drip 输液器（60 gtts/mL）以标准维持速度 75 mL/hr 输液。滴速是多少？

options.en: 8 gtts/min
options.zh: 8 gtts/min

options.en: 13 gtts/min
options.zh: 13 gtts/min

options.en: 45 gtts/min
options.zh: 45 gtts/min

options.en: 75 gtts/min
options.zh: 75 gtts/min

questions.explanationEn: 75 mL x 60 gtts/mL / 60 minutes = 4500 / 60 = 75 gtts/min.
