With a micro-drip set, gtts/min always equals mL/hr. 13 gtts/min would be the answer with a 10 gtts/mL macro set - a micro-drip is often preferred in frail elderly patients because it makes accidental over-infusion harder.
questions.explanationZh: 75 mL x 60 gtts/mL / 60 分钟 = 4500 / 60 = 75 gtts/min。用 micro-drip 时 gtts/min 数值恒等于 mL/hr。13 gtts/min 是 10 gtts/mL macro 输液器的答案——体弱老年病人常首选 micro-drip，因为它更不容易发生意外过量输注。

questions.questionEn: A 68-year-old woman (70 kg) with a history of CHF is hypotensive at 82/50 after two days of vomiting. The hypovolemia protocol allows a 20 mL/kg bolus to a maximum of 2 litres. What is the safest way to run this bolus?
questions.questionZh: 一名有 CHF 病史的 68 岁女性（70 kg）呕吐两天后血压 82/50。Hypovolemia protocol 允许 20 mL/kg、最多 2 升的液体冲击。最安全的执行方式是什么？

options.en: Run the full calculated 1400 mL wide open without stopping, since the protocol allows it
options.zh: 既然 protocol 允许，就一次性全开输完计算出的 1400 mL

options.en: Withhold all fluid because CHF is an absolute contraindication to IV therapy
options.zh: CHF 是静脉输液的绝对禁忌，一滴都不能给

options.en: Give the bolus with reassessment every 500 mL as the protocol directs - and in a CHF patient specifically recheck breath sounds and work of breathing at each interval, stopping if congestion develops
options.zh: 按 protocol 每 500 mL 重新评估一次——对 CHF 病人尤其要在每个间隔复查呼吸音和呼吸做功，一旦出现淤血征象即停止

options.en: Give 250 mL total regardless of response, then switch to TKVO
options.zh: 无论反应如何都只给 250 mL，然后改为 TKVO

questions.explanationEn: The protocol's own safeguard - reassessing every 500 mL - exists precisely for patients with limited cardiac reserve. Her calculated bolus is 20 x 70 = 1400 mL, but in CHF each increment demands auscultation for crackles and reassessment of breathing before continuing. Dehydration and CHF can coexist; neither blind full-volume infusion nor blanket fluid refusal is correct.
questions.explanationZh: Protocol 自带的安全机制——每 500 mL 重评——正是为心脏储备有限的病人设计的。她的计算量是 20 x 70 = 1400 mL，但对 CHF 病人，每一段输注前都要听诊有无湿啰音并重评呼吸。脱水与 CHF 可以并存；盲目全量输注和一概拒绝补液都不正确。

questions.questionEn: The Pediatric Assessment Triangle (PAT) allows a rapid 'from the doorway' impression of a sick child. What are its three arms?
questions.questionZh: Pediatric Assessment Triangle（儿科评估三角，PAT）可以在「门口第一眼」快速形成对患儿的总体印象。它的三条边是什么？

options.en: Airway patency, blood pressure, and temperature
options.zh: 气道通畅度、血压和体温

options.en: Appearance, work of breathing, and circulation to the skin
options.zh: 外观（appearance）、呼吸做功（work of breathing）和皮肤循环（circulation to skin）

options.en: Alertness, verbal response, and pain response
options.zh: 警觉、言语反应和疼痛反应

options.en: Pulse, pupils, and skin colour
options.zh: 脉搏、瞳孔和肤色

questions.explanationEn: The PAT is a hands-off first impression built from appearance (tone, interactiveness, consolability, look or gaze, speech or cry), work of breathing (retractions, positioning, audible sounds), and circulation to skin (pallor, mottling, cyanosis). It precedes and complements the hands-on primary survey.
questions.explanationZh: PAT 是不动手的第一印象，由三部分构成：外观（肌张力、互动性、可安抚性、眼神、言语/哭声）、呼吸做功（凹陷、体位、可闻及的呼吸音）和皮肤循环（苍白、花斑、发绀）。它先于并补充动手进行的 primary survey。

questions.questionEn: You enter a home to find an 18-month-old girl lying limp across her mother's lap. She makes no eye contact, does not resist your exam, and gives a weak intermittent whimper. Using PAT reasoning, this presentation indicates:
questions.questionZh: 你进入住宅，看到一名 18 个月大的女孩软软地横躺在母亲腿上。她没有眼神接触，不抗拒你的检查，只发出微弱断续的呜咽。按 PAT 推理，这种表现提示：

options.en: A seriously ill child - abnormal appearance (poor tone, no interactiveness) signals inadequate brain perfusion or oxygenation regardless of the eventual diagnosis
options.zh: 重症患儿——外观异常（肌张力差、无互动）提示脑灌注或氧合不足，无论最终诊断是什么

options.en: A tired toddler who missed her nap and needs no further assessment
options.zh: 只是错过午睡的疲倦幼儿，无需进一步评估

options.en: Normal stranger anxiety for her age
options.zh: 该年龄段正常的陌生人焦虑

options.en: A well child because she is quiet and cooperative with the exam
options.zh: 安静配合检查，说明是健康孩子

questions.explanationEn: A toddler who is limp, uninterested in strangers, and does not resist examination is displaying abnormal appearance - the most sensitive PAT arm. Healthy 18-month-olds typically fear strangers and fight the exam; 'easy to examine' in this age group is a red flag, not reassurance. She needs a full primary survey, oxygen consideration, and prompt transport.
questions.explanationZh: 软弱无力、对陌生人毫无兴趣、不抗拒检查的幼儿属于外观异常——PAT 中最敏感的一条边。健康的 18 个月幼儿通常怕生并抗拒检查；这个年龄「很好检查」是危险信号而不是好消息。她需要完整 primary survey、考虑给氧并尽快转运。

questions.questionEn: When assessing for a pulse in an unresponsive infant, which site does the BC guideline direct you to use?
questions.questionZh: 评估无反应婴儿的脉搏时，BC 指南要求使用哪个部位？

options.en: Carotid artery
options.zh: 颈动脉

options.en: Radial artery
options.zh: 桡动脉

options.en: Brachial artery
options.zh: 肱动脉

options.en: Dorsalis pedis artery
options.zh: 足背动脉

questions.explanationEn: The infant CPR basics state: assess for a pulse using the brachial rather than the carotid artery. An infant's short, chubby neck makes the carotid difficult and unreliable to palpate; the brachial site on the inner upper arm is accessible and accurate.
questions.explanationZh: 婴儿 CPR 基础要点指出：应触诊肱动脉而非颈动脉。婴儿脖颈短而多肉，颈动脉难以可靠触及；上臂内侧的肱动脉既好找又准确。

questions.questionEn: Why does the BC guideline recommend placing a pad under an infant's shoulders during CPR or airway management?
questions.questionZh: 为什么 BC 指南建议在 CPR 或气道管理时于婴儿肩下垫一块垫料？

options.en: To raise the chest for easier compressions
options.zh: 抬高胸部便于按压

options.en: To keep the infant warm during resuscitation
options.zh: 在复苏中为婴儿保暖

options.en: To make the infant more visible to the second rescuer
options.zh: 让第二名施救者更容易看到婴儿

options.en: The infant's proportionally large head flexes the neck when supine - shoulder padding restores a neutral airway position
options.zh: 婴儿头部占身体比例大，仰卧时会使颈部前屈——肩下垫料可恢复气道中立位

questions.explanationEn: Due to the size of an infant's head relative to the body, lying flat pushes the neck into flexion and can obstruct the airway. A pad under the shoulders (if available) facilitates the neutral position, keeping the airway open - a uniquely pediatric anatomical adaptation.
questions.explanationZh: 婴儿头部相对躯干偏大，平躺时颈部会被推向前屈，可能压闭气道。肩下垫料（如有）帮助维持中立位、保持气道开放——这是儿科特有的解剖学调整。

questions.questionEn: You and your partner are performing CPR on an 8-month-old infant. What compression-to-ventilation ratio should you use?
questions.questionZh: 你和搭档正在对一名 8 个月大的婴儿实施 CPR。应采用什么按压通气比？

options.en: 30:2, the same as for adults
options.zh: 30:2——与成人相同

options.en: 15:2, the two-rescuer ratio for infants and children
options.zh: 15:2——婴儿和儿童的双人施救比例

options.en: 3:1 with continuous compressions
options.zh: 3:1 并持续按压

options.en: 5:1 alternating rescuers each cycle
options.zh: 5:1，每个循环轮换施救者

questions.explanationEn: For infants and children the ratio is 30:2 with one rescuer but 15:2 with two rescuers - the extra ventilations reflect the primarily asphyxial nature of pediatric arrest. The 3:1 ratio is reserved for neonates (up to 28 days). Compression rate stays 100-120/min, depth one-third to one-half of chest diameter.
questions.explanationZh: 婴儿和儿童单人施救为 30:2，双人施救为 15:2——更多通气对应儿科心搏骤停以窒息为主的本质。3:1 仅用于新生儿（出生 28 天内）。按压频率仍为 100-120 次/分，深度为胸廓前后径的 1/3 至 1/2。

questions.questionEn: A 4-month-old with bronchiolitis is mottled and barely responsive. The brachial pulse is present but slow - you count 50 beats per minute. Breathing is shallow and gasping. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 一名患毛细支气管炎的 4 个月婴儿出现皮肤花斑、几乎无反应。肱动脉搏动存在但缓慢——数得每分钟 50 次。呼吸浅慢伴喘息样呼吸。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Begin CPR - an infant with a heart rate below 60 and signs of poor perfusion is treated as being in arrest
options.zh: 开始 CPR——心率低于 60 且伴灌注不良征象的婴儿按心搏骤停处理

options.en: Withhold CPR because a palpable pulse always contraindicates compressions
options.zh: 不做 CPR——只要摸得到脉搏就禁忌按压

options.en: Provide ventilations only and recheck the pulse in 10 minutes
options.zh: 只做通气，10 分钟后再查脉搏

options.en: Apply the AED first and wait for its analysis before touching the chest
options.zh: 先贴 AED，等待分析结果后再碰胸部

questions.explanationEn: The pediatric guideline directs starting CPR if there is no pulse or if the heart rate is below 60 with signs of poor perfusion (pallor, mottling, cyanosis, decreased LOC). In infants, cardiac output is heavily rate-dependent; a rate of 50 with mottling and decreased responsiveness cannot sustain perfusion. This is a key difference from adult practice.
questions.explanationZh: 儿科指南要求：无脉搏、或心率低于 60 且伴灌注不良征象（苍白、花斑、发绀、意识下降）时即开始 CPR。婴儿的心输出量高度依赖心率；心率 50 加上花斑和反应下降无法维持灌注。这是与成人实践的关键差异。

questions.questionEn: Off duty and without a phone, you find a 3-year-old unresponsive and pulseless at a playground. Nobody saw what happened and you are alone. What does the guideline direct?
questions.questionZh: 你下班且没带手机，在游乐场发现一名 3 岁儿童无反应、无脉搏。无人目击经过，现场只有你一人。指南要求怎么做？

options.en: Leave immediately to find a phone, then return to start CPR
options.zh: 立即离开去找电话，回来后再开始 CPR

options.en: Perform rescue breathing only until help happens to arrive
options.zh: 只做人工呼吸，直到碰巧有人来帮忙

options.en: Perform about 2 minutes (5 cycles) of CPR first, then activate the emergency response system and get an AED
options.zh: 先做约 2 分钟（5 个循环）CPR，再启动急救系统并获取 AED

options.en: Do compressions for 10 minutes before considering leaving the child
options.zh: 先按压 10 分钟再考虑离开孩子

questions.explanationEn: For an unwitnessed pediatric collapse when alone, the guideline directs 5 cycles (about 2 minutes) of CPR before activating the emergency response system, because pediatric arrests are usually asphyxial and immediate CPR addresses the primary problem. Had the collapse been witnessed, you would activate the system and get an AED first.
questions.explanationZh: 单人面对无目击的儿科倒地，指南要求先做 5 个循环（约 2 分钟）CPR 再启动急救系统，因为儿科骤停多为窒息性，立即 CPR 针对的正是根本问题。若倒地被目击，则应先启动系统并取 AED。

questions.questionEn: A 12-year-old is struck in the centre of the chest by a line drive at a baseball game and collapses immediately in front of a crowd. You are first on scene with a bystander beside you. Why does this situation demand the AED as early as possible?
questions.questionZh: 棒球比赛中，一名 12 岁少年胸部正中被平飞球击中后当众立即倒地。你第一个到场，旁边有一名旁观者。为什么这种情况要求尽早使用 AED？

options.en: All pediatric arrests are shockable, so the AED always takes precedence over CPR
options.zh: 所有儿科骤停都可电击，AED 永远优先于 CPR

options.en: The AED is needed mainly to document the rhythm for the hospital
options.zh: AED 主要用于为医院记录心律

options.en: AED use prevents the need for chest compressions in commotio cordis
options.zh: 用了 AED 就不需要做胸外按压了

options.en: A blow to the precordium followed by collapse suggests commotio cordis - one of the rare pediatric situations where ventricular fibrillation is likely, making early defibrillation decisive; send the bystander for the AED while you start CPR
options.zh: 心前区被击中后立即倒地提示 commotio cordis——儿科少见的室颤高概率情形之一，早期除颤起决定作用；让旁观者去取 AED，你立即开始 CPR

questions.explanationEn: Most pediatric arrests are asphyxial, but the guideline notes VF occurs in children with previous cardiac problems, electrocution, or a sharp blow to the precordial area followed by collapse (commotio cordis). This witnessed sudden arrest fits the VF pattern, so immediate activation and early AED matter, with CPR ongoing - defibrillation and compressions coexist, neither replacing the other.
questions.explanationZh: 儿科骤停多为窒息性，但指南指出：有心脏病史、电击伤、或心前区被猛击后倒地（commotio cordis）的儿童可能出现室颤。这种被目击的骤然倒地符合室颤模式，因此立即启动系统和尽早 AED 至关重要，同时持续 CPR——除颤与按压并行，互不取代。

questions.questionEn: You record a heart rate of 130 and a respiratory rate of 38 in a settled 6-month-old with a mild fever. How should you interpret these numbers?
questions.questionZh: 你为一名安静、低热的 6 个月婴儿测得心率 130、呼吸 38 次/分。应如何解读这些数值？

options.en: Both are dangerously high and indicate decompensated shock
options.zh: 两项都危险偏高，提示失代偿性休克

options.en: The heart rate is normal but the respiratory rate indicates respiratory failure
options.zh: 心率正常，但呼吸频率提示呼吸衰竭

options.en: Both fall within the expected range for a 6-month-old - infant norms are much faster than adult norms
options.zh: 两项都在 6 个月婴儿的正常范围内——婴儿的正常值远高于成人

options.en: Both are too low for this age and suggest impending arrest
options.zh: 对这个年龄来说两项都偏低，提示即将骤停

questions.explanationEn: Infants normally run heart rates of roughly 100-160 and respiratory rates of roughly 30-60. Applying adult thresholds to children is a classic exam trap in both directions: an infant heart rate of 130 is normal, while an infant rate below 60 with poor perfusion is an indication to start CPR.
questions.explanationZh: 婴儿正常心率约 100-160 次/分，呼吸约 30-60 次/分。把成人标准套用到儿童身上是经典考试陷阱，两个方向都会错：婴儿心率 130 属正常，而婴儿心率低于 60 且灌注不良则是开始 CPR 的指征。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.43; p.18 (References: Nancy Caroline)

questions.questionEn: A 2-year-old with a two-day history of vomiting and diarrhea is alert but quiet. His hands are cool and mottled to the wrists, capillary refill is 4 seconds, and the radial pulse is weak but present. His blood pressure is 92/60. What does this picture indicate?
questions.questionZh: 一名 2 岁儿童呕吐腹泻两天，神志清楚但安静。双手至腕部发凉、有花斑，毛细血管再充盈 4 秒，桡动脉搏动微弱但可及，血压 92/60。这幅图景提示什么？

options.en: He is well perfused - a normal blood pressure excludes shock in children
options.zh: 灌注良好——儿童血压正常即可排除休克

options.en: Compensated shock - abnormal skin circulation and delayed capillary refill precede hypotension in children
options.zh: 代偿性休克——儿童的皮肤循环异常和毛细血管再充盈延迟出现在低血压之前

options.en: Simple dehydration requiring only oral fluids at home
options.zh: 单纯脱水，在家口服补液即可

options.en: Cold exposure, since mottling is only an environmental sign
options.zh: 受凉所致——花斑只是环境因素造成的

questions.explanationEn: Children maintain blood pressure far longer than adults by vasoconstricting and increasing heart rate; the circulation-to-skin arm of the PAT (mottling, pallor, delayed refill) therefore turns abnormal well before the blood pressure drops. A normal pediatric BP never excludes shock - when it finally falls, the child is decompensating.
questions.explanationZh: 儿童通过血管收缩和心率增快维持血压的时间远长于成人；因此 PAT 中「皮肤循环」这一边（花斑、苍白、再充盈延迟）在血压下降之前就已异常。儿童血压正常绝不能排除休克——等血压真的降下来时，孩子已经在失代偿了。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.54; p.18 (References: Nancy Caroline)

questions.questionEn: A 7-year-old was struck by a car at approximately 40 km/h while crossing the street. He is crying, moving all limbs, and has an abrasion on his flank with vitals in normal range for age. Your transport decision should be:
questions.questionZh: 一名 7 岁儿童过马路时被时速约 40 km/h 的汽车撞倒。他在哭、四肢均能活动，腰侧有擦伤，vitals 在该年龄正常范围。你的转运决策应是：

options.en: Stable - crying children are always well perfused and low risk
options.zh: 稳定——会哭的孩子灌注一定良好、风险低

options.en: Stable - normal vitals in a child rule out significant internal injury
options.zh: 稳定——儿童 vitals 正常即可排除明显内伤

options.en: Stable unless he vomits during your assessment
options.zh: 稳定——除非评估期间发生呕吐

options.en: Unstable - auto versus pedestrian at over 30 km/h is a high-risk mechanism, and a child's compact body transmits force to multiple organs
options.zh: 不稳定——汽车撞行人且车速超过 30 km/h 属于高危机制，而儿童身体紧凑，外力会传导至多个器官

questions.explanationEn: The mechanism criterion of auto versus pedestrian or cyclist at over 30 km/h applies at any age. In children the same energy is distributed across a smaller body with less fat and a more pliable rib cage, so multi-system injury is common and serious internal injury can exist behind normal-looking vitals and intact skin.
questions.explanationZh: 「汽车撞行人/骑车人且车速超过 30 km/h」这条机制标准适用于任何年龄。儿童体型更小、脂肪更少、胸廓更柔韧，同样的能量会分布到多个系统，因此多系统损伤常见，严重内伤可能藏在看似正常的 vitals 和完好的皮肤之下。

questions.questionEn: A 20 kg child is hypotensive after significant blood loss. Using the BC fluid bolus of 20 mL/kg, what volume should you plan for the first bolus?
questions.questionZh: 一名 20 kg 儿童在明显失血后出现低血压。按 BC 的 20 mL/kg 液体冲击量，第一次 bolus 应计划输入多少？

options.en: 400 mL
options.zh: 400 mL

options.en: 200 mL
options.zh: 200 mL

options.en: 2000 mL, the protocol maximum
options.zh: 2000 mL —— protocol 上限

questions.explanationEn: 20 mL/kg x 20 kg = 400 mL. The 2 litre figure is the maximum for the protocol, not a pediatric dose - giving it to a 20 kg child would be a five-fold overdose. Reassess after the bolus; the protocol also directs reassessment every 500 mL, which in a small child means reassessing well before that mark is reached.
questions.explanationZh: 20 mL/kg x 20 kg = 400 mL。2 升是 protocol 的最大值，不是儿科剂量——给 20 kg 儿童输 2 升是五倍过量。Bolus 后要重新评估；protocol 要求每 500 mL 重评，对小体重儿童意味着远在到达该数值之前就应重评。

questions.questionEn: A frightened 4-year-old with a forearm injury screams and pulls away whenever you approach. Which approach best allows you to complete an accurate assessment?
questions.questionZh: 一名前臂受伤、受惊吓的 4 岁儿童，每次你靠近都尖叫躲闪。哪种方式最有利于完成准确评估？

options.en: Have two crew members hold the child still so the exam can be completed quickly
options.zh: 让两名队员按住孩子，以便快速完成检查

options.en: Assess at the child's eye level with the caregiver holding him, start with the uninjured side, and examine the painful area last
options.zh: 蹲到与孩子平视的高度，让照护者抱着他，从未受伤的一侧开始检查，把疼痛部位放到最后

options.en: Separate the child from the parent to remove distractions
options.zh: 把孩子和家长分开，以减少干扰

options.en: Skip the hands-on exam entirely and rely on the parent's description
options.zh: 完全跳过体格检查，仅依赖家长描述

questions.explanationEn: A struggling, screaming child yields unreliable findings. Keeping the caregiver present, working at eye level, and moving toe-to-head or uninjured-to-injured preserves trust and produces a more complete examination. Restraint is reserved for immediate safety needs; separating a preschooler from the caregiver reliably worsens cooperation.
questions.explanationZh: 挣扎尖叫的孩子给出的检查结果不可靠。让照护者陪在身边、蹲到平视高度、从脚到头或从健侧到患侧推进，可以维持信任并获得更完整的检查。强行按住只保留给即刻安全需要；把学龄前儿童与照护者分开一定会让配合度更差。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.9; p.18 (References: Nancy Caroline)

questions.questionEn: A 5-year-old with severe asthma has been working hard to breathe for an hour. Over ten minutes his respiratory rate falls from 44 to 18, his wheeze becomes quiet, and he stops fighting the oxygen mask. What does this change mean?
questions.questionZh: 一名 5 岁重度哮喘患儿已经费力呼吸一小时。十分钟内他的呼吸频率从 44 降到 18，哮鸣音变轻，也不再抗拒氧气面罩。这种变化意味着什么？

options.en: The salbutamol is working and he is improving
options.zh: 沙丁胺醇起效了，他在好转

options.en: He is falling asleep normally after exhaustion from crying
options.zh: 他哭累了，正常入睡

options.en: Impending respiratory failure - a falling rate, quiet chest, and decreasing responsiveness mean he is tiring and needs assisted ventilation, not reassurance
options.zh: 即将发生呼吸衰竭——呼吸频率下降、胸部安静、反应性降低说明他已力竭，需要辅助通气而不是安慰

options.en: He no longer needs oxygen because his work of breathing has decreased
options.zh: 呼吸做功减少，说明他不再需要氧气

questions.explanationEn: A silent chest with a falling respiratory rate and decreasing level of consciousness in an asthmatic child signals exhaustion and impending arrest, not improvement - air movement has become too poor to generate wheeze. The primary survey intervention indications include assisting inadequate or failing respirations when respirations are abnormally slow or shallow with decreasing LOC or cyanosis.
questions.explanationZh: 哮喘患儿出现「安静胸」伴呼吸频率下降和意识水平降低，是力竭与即将骤停的信号而非好转——气流已弱到无法产生哮鸣音。Primary survey 干预指征中明确包括：呼吸异常缓慢或表浅、伴意识下降或发绀时，应辅助通气。

questions.questionEn: How long may suction be applied in a pediatric patient and in an infant according to the BC guidelines?
questions.questionZh: 根据 BC 指南，儿童和婴儿的每次吸痰时间上限分别是多少？

options.en: 10 seconds in the pediatric patient and 5 seconds in an infant
options.zh: 儿童 10 秒，婴儿 5 秒

options.en: 15 seconds in the pediatric patient and 10 seconds in an infant
options.zh: 儿童 15 秒，婴儿 10 秒

options.en: 20 seconds for both
options.zh: 两者均为 20 秒

options.en: 5 seconds in the pediatric patient and 3 seconds in an infant
options.zh: 儿童 5 秒，婴儿 3 秒

questions.explanationEn: The guideline specifies 10-15 seconds in the adult, 10 seconds in the pediatric patient, and 5 seconds in an infant. Shorter times reflect smaller oxygen reserves and higher metabolic demand - prolonged suctioning causes hypoxia and bradycardia in small children.
questions.explanationZh: 指南规定：成人 10-15 秒，儿童 10 秒，婴儿 5 秒。时间更短是因为氧储备更小、代谢需求更高——吸引时间过长会使幼儿出现低氧和心动过缓。

questions.questionEn: A conscious 9-month-old choked on a grape. He cannot cry or cough and is turning blue. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 一名 9 个月大的清醒婴儿被葡萄噎住，无法哭也无法咳嗽，面色发绀。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Perform abdominal thrusts as you would for an adult
options.zh: 像对成人一样实施腹部冲击

options.en: Perform a blind finger sweep to retrieve the grape
options.zh: 盲目手指清扫以取出葡萄

options.en: Encourage him to cough forcefully and monitor closely
options.zh: 鼓励他用力咳嗽并密切观察

options.en: Deliver repeated cycles of 5 back blows followed by 5 chest compressions until the object is expelled
options.zh: 反复循环给予 5 次拍背和 5 次胸部按压，直到异物排出

questions.explanationEn: For an infant with a complete obstruction the guideline directs repeated cycles of 5 back blows followed by 5 chest compressions. Abdominal thrusts are described for conscious adults and children over 1 year of age, not infants. Blind finger sweeps are explicitly prohibited, and encouraging coughing applies only to a partial obstruction where the infant can still move air.
questions.explanationZh: 对完全气道梗阻的婴儿，指南要求反复循环给予 5 次拍背和 5 次胸部按压。腹部冲击适用于清醒的成人和 1 岁以上儿童，不适用于婴儿。盲目手指清扫被明确禁止；鼓励咳嗽只适用于仍有气流的部分梗阻。

questions.questionEn: You are resuscitating a 5-year-old in cardiac arrest and your AED kit contains only adult pads. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 你正在为一名 5 岁心搏骤停患儿实施复苏，AED 套件里只有成人电极片。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Do not use the AED at all - adult pads are contraindicated under 8 years of age
options.zh: 完全不用 AED——8 岁以下禁用成人电极片

options.en: Use the adult pads and deliver the adult joules
options.zh: 使用成人电极片并按成人能量除颤

options.en: Cut the adult pads in half to reduce the delivered energy
options.zh: 把成人电极片剪成一半以减少输出能量

options.en: Wait for another unit to arrive with pediatric pads before analyzing
options.zh: 等另一辆车送来儿科电极片后再分析心律

questions.explanationEn: The guideline states that for a child 0-8 years switch to child AED pads if available, and if not available you may use the adult pads and deliver the adult joules. Delaying or withholding defibrillation is far more harmful than a slightly higher energy dose. Never modify pads.
questions.explanationZh: 指南规定：0-8 岁儿童如有儿科电极片则更换使用，若没有，可以使用成人电极片并给予成人能量。延误或放弃除颤的危害远大于稍高的能量剂量。绝不可裁剪或改造电极片。

questions.questionEn: Placing AED pads on a small 2-year-old in arrest, you see that in the standard anterior/lateral position the two pads are almost touching - about 2 cm apart. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 为一名体型瘦小的 2 岁骤停患儿贴 AED 电极片时，你发现按标准前/侧位放置后两片几乎相碰——间距约 2 cm。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Leave them as placed since the position is standard
options.zh: 维持原位——这是标准位置

options.en: Overlap the pads so both make full skin contact
options.zh: 让两片重叠，确保都完全贴合皮肤

options.en: Shift to an anterior/posterior configuration, since pads within 2.5 cm of each other may need repositioning
options.zh: 改为前/后位放置——两片间距小于 2.5 cm 时可能需要重新放置

options.en: Trim one pad so it fits alongside the other
options.zh: 剪小其中一片，使两片能并排放下

questions.explanationEn: The guideline states that if pads in the normal anterior/lateral chest position are within 2.5 cm (one inch) of each other, they may need to be shifted to an anterior/posterior configuration. Pads that touch or overlap allow current to arc between them across the skin rather than through the heart.
questions.explanationZh: 指南规定：若按常规前/侧位放置时两片间距在 2.5 cm（1 英寸）以内，可能需要改为前/后位放置。电极片相碰或重叠会让电流沿皮肤在两片之间「短路」，而不是穿过心脏。

questions.questionEn: You are managing a 3-year-old in cardiac arrest after a near-drowning. CPR is in progress with an SGA in place. Regarding intra-arrest transport, which statement reflects the BC guideline?
questions.questionZh: 你正在处理一名溺水后心搏骤停的 3 岁儿童，CPR 进行中且已置入 SGA。关于「骤停中转运」，哪种说法符合 BC 指南？

options.en: Transport with ongoing CPR is never permitted because compressions deteriorate during movement
options.zh: 绝不允许边 CPR 边转运，因为搬动会使按压质量下降

options.en: Pediatric arrests must always be worked on scene for the full 30 minutes before any movement
options.zh: 儿科骤停必须在现场做满 30 分钟才能搬动

options.en: Transport should begin immediately in all arrests to reach definitive care faster
options.zh: 所有骤停都应立即转运以尽快获得确定性治疗

options.en: CPR is most effective while stationary, but intra-arrest transport with ongoing CPR may occur for pediatrics, hypothermia, trauma, or treatable causes - and this case fits both criteria
options.zh: CPR 在静止时最有效，但儿科、低体温、创伤或可逆病因的骤停可以边 CPR 边转运——本例同时符合两条

questions.explanationEn: The guideline acknowledges CPR is more effective while stationary, yet explicitly lists paediatrics, hypothermic, traumatic, and treatable causes as situations where intra-arrest transport with ongoing CPR may occur. A drowning arrest is hypoxic and potentially reversible, so this child meets the criteria twice over.
questions.explanationZh: 指南承认 CPR 在静止时更有效，但明确列出儿科、低体温、创伤和可逆病因是可以边 CPR 边转运的情形。溺水骤停属于缺氧性、潜在可逆，因此这名患儿同时符合两条标准。

questions.questionEn: A 2-year-old with a febrile illness lies still, does not open his eyes when his mother calls him, but cries and pushes your hand away when you insert an IV. Using AVPU, he is:
questions.questionZh: 一名发热患病的 2 岁儿童安静躺着，母亲呼唤时不睁眼，但你穿刺静脉时他哭闹并推开你的手。按 AVPU 他属于：

options.en: P - responsive to pain only; monitor the airway closely and position semi-prone if injuries permit
options.zh: P —— 仅对疼痛有反应；需严密监测气道，如损伤允许置于 semi-prone 体位

options.en: V - crying counts as a verbal response
options.zh: V —— 哭泣算作言语反应

options.en: A - he is alert because he responded purposefully
options.zh: A —— 他有目的地反应，属于 alert

options.en: U - toddlers cannot be scored on AVPU
options.zh: U —— 幼儿无法用 AVPU 评分

questions.explanationEn: Response only to a painful stimulus is P regardless of age; crying triggered by the IV is a response to pain, not to voice. The guideline warns that a patient at P must have the airway monitored closely with intervention as necessary, and be positioned semi-prone if injuries permit. Failing to respond to a parent's voice is a serious finding in a toddler.
questions.explanationZh: 只对疼痛刺激有反应，无论年龄都评为 P；穿刺引发的哭泣是对疼痛而非对言语的反应。指南提示 P 级病人必须严密监测气道并按需干预，如损伤允许摆 semi-prone 体位。幼儿对母亲呼唤没有反应本身就是严重发现。

questions.questionEn: A 9-year-old with pneumonia has an SpO2 of 90% on oxygen, a respiratory rate of 34, and accessory muscle use. He is awake and following commands. Can you apply CPAP?
questions.questionZh: 一名 9 岁肺炎患儿吸氧下 SpO2 90%、呼吸 34 次/分、有辅助呼吸肌使用，清醒且能遵嘱。可以给他上 CPAP 吗？

options.en: Yes - he meets the RR, SpO2, and accessory muscle criteria
options.zh: 可以——他符合 RR、SpO2 和辅助肌使用三项标准

options.en: No - CPAP is contraindicated in patients 12 years of age and under; support him with oxygen and assisted ventilation as needed
options.zh: 不可以——CPAP 对 12 岁及以下病人属禁忌；应给氧并按需辅助通气

options.en: Yes, but only at a maximum of 5 cmH2O
options.zh: 可以，但最大只能用 5 cmH2O

options.en: Yes - pneumonia is a listed CPAP indication at any age
options.zh: 可以——肺炎在任何年龄都是 CPAP 的指征

questions.explanationEn: CPAP is indicated for patients 13 years of age and older, and patients 12 years and under are listed as a contraindication - even when the RR, SpO2, and accessory muscle criteria are met and pneumonia is otherwise a valid indication. Manage this child with oxygen titration and BVM assistance if he deteriorates.
questions.explanationZh: CPAP 的指征是 13 岁及以上，12 岁及以下明确列为禁忌——即使 RR、SpO2 和辅助肌使用三项标准都符合、且肺炎本身是有效指征也不行。该患儿应通过滴定给氧处理，若恶化则用 BVM 辅助通气。

questions.questionEn: You must deliver a 300 mL fluid bolus to a 15 kg child over 20 minutes using a 10 gtts/mL set. What drip rate is required?
questions.questionZh: 需要用 10 gtts/mL 输液器在 20 分钟内为一名 15 kg 儿童输入 300 mL 液体冲击量。所需滴速是多少？

options.en: 50 gtts/min
options.zh: 50 gtts/min

options.en: 100 gtts/min
options.zh: 100 gtts/min

options.en: 150 gtts/min
options.zh: 150 gtts/min

options.en: 30 gtts/min
options.zh: 30 gtts/min

questions.explanationEn: 300 mL x 10 gtts/mL / 20 minutes = 3000 / 20 = 150 gtts/min. That is roughly 2-3 drops per second - a rate this fast is a signal to watch the bag closely and reassess the child frequently, since 300 mL represents the full 20 mL/kg bolus for a 15 kg child.
questions.explanationZh: 300 mL x 10 gtts/mL / 20 分钟 = 3000 / 20 = 150 gtts/min，约每秒 2-3 滴。这么快的速度提示必须紧盯液袋并频繁重评患儿，因为 300 mL 正是 15 kg 儿童 20 mL/kg 的完整冲击量。

questions.questionEn: A 6-year-old fell from a play structure onto a paved surface. Beyond the height of the fall, which history details does the BC critical history list direct you to obtain?
questions.questionZh: 一名 6 岁儿童从游乐设施上摔到水泥地面。除坠落高度外，BC 的 critical history 清单还要求收集哪些信息？

options.en: The manufacturer and installation date of the play structure
options.zh: 游乐设施的生产厂家和安装日期

options.en: Whether the school has an incident report policy
options.zh: 学校是否有事故报告制度

options.en: The child's immunization record and school grade
options.zh: 孩子的疫苗接种记录和年级

options.en: Whether it was a free fall or he hit objects on the way down, the landing surface, what body part hit first, his position and condition afterward, any loss of consciousness, and the cause of the fall
options.zh: 是自由坠落还是途中撞到物体、落地面材质、先着地的部位、坠落后的位置与状态、有无意识丧失，以及跌倒原因

questions.explanationEn: The fall history list specifies where from, height, free fall or striking objects, landing surface, position at impact and what hit first, initial position and condition, whether the patient has been moved, loss of consciousness, and the cause of the fall. First point of impact predicts the injury pattern - a head-first landing on pavement demands different vigilance than feet-first.
questions.explanationZh: 跌倒的 critical history 清单包括：从哪里坠落、高度、是否自由坠落或途中撞击、落地面、撞击时体位与先着地部位、初始位置与状态、是否被移动过、有无意识丧失、以及跌倒原因。先着地部位可预测损伤模式——头先着地于水泥面与脚先着地需要完全不同的警惕重点。

questions.questionEn: An 11-month-old with a cough has audible grunting on expiration, head bobbing with each breath, and intercostal retractions. His SpO2 is 91% and he is alert. What is your interpretation and priority?
questions.questionZh: 一名 11 个月大、有咳嗽的婴儿，呼气时可闻及呻吟（grunting），每次呼吸伴点头样动作，有肋间凹陷。SpO2 91%，神志清楚。你的判断和优先处置是什么？

options.en: Grunting and head bobbing are signs of severe respiratory distress in an infant - give oxygen, minimize agitation, and transport promptly with continuous reassessment
options.zh: 呻吟和点头样呼吸是婴儿重度呼吸窘迫的表现——应给氧、尽量减少刺激、持续复评并尽快转运

options.en: Grunting is a normal infant sound and requires no intervention
options.zh: 呻吟是婴儿的正常发声，无需处理

options.en: Because he is alert and his SpO2 is above 90%, no oxygen is needed
options.zh: 他神志清楚且 SpO2 高于 90%，不需要给氧

options.en: Head bobbing indicates a neurological problem rather than a respiratory one
options.zh: 点头样动作提示神经系统问题而非呼吸问题

questions.explanationEn: Grunting is an infant's attempt to generate self-PEEP against collapsing alveoli, and head bobbing reflects accessory muscle recruitment - both are the work-of-breathing arm of the PAT turning abnormal and both mark severe distress. Respiratory distress is a listed oxygen indication; agitation increases oxygen demand, so handle the infant gently and transport without delay.
questions.explanationZh: 呻吟是婴儿对抗肺泡塌陷、自造 PEEP 的表现，点头样动作反映辅助呼吸肌动员——两者都是 PAT 中「呼吸做功」这条边异常的信号，均代表重度窘迫。呼吸窘迫是明确的给氧指征；哭闹烦躁会增加耗氧，因此应轻柔操作并立即转运。

questions.questionEn: What compression rate and depth does the BC guideline specify for CPR on a 6-year-old?
questions.questionZh: BC 指南规定对 6 岁儿童实施 CPR 的按压频率和深度是多少？

options.en: 80-100 per minute at a fixed depth of 5 cm
options.zh: 每分钟 80-100 次，固定深度 5 cm

options.en: 100-120 per minute at a depth of one-third to one-half the chest diameter
options.zh: 每分钟 100-120 次，深度为胸廓前后径的三分之一至二分之一

options.en: 60-80 per minute at a depth of 2 cm
options.zh: 每分钟 60-80 次，深度 2 cm

options.en: 120-140 per minute at a depth of 6 cm
options.zh: 每分钟 120-140 次，深度 6 cm

questions.explanationEn: For infants and children the optimum rate is 100-120 per minute with a depth of one-third to one-half the chest diameter. The rate matches adults; the depth is expressed proportionally because a fixed 5-6 cm target would be dangerous in a small chest. Allow complete recoil after each compression and keep interruptions under 5 seconds.
questions.explanationZh: 婴儿和儿童的最佳按压频率为每分钟 100-120 次，深度为胸廓前后径的 1/3 至 1/2。频率与成人一致；深度按比例表述，因为对小胸廓固定 5-6 cm 会造成危险。每次按压后要完全回弹，中断保持在 5 秒以内。

questions.questionEn: A baby born 3 hours ago requires CPR. What compression-to-ventilation ratio applies, and what is the role of the AED?
questions.questionZh: 一名出生 3 小时的新生儿需要 CPR。应采用什么按压通气比？AED 起什么作用？

options.en: 15:2 with the AED applied as soon as available
options.zh: 15:2，AED 一旦可用立即使用

options.en: 30:2 with the AED applied after 2 minutes
options.zh: 30:2，2 分钟后使用 AED

options.en: 3:1, and no AED is used in the neonate
options.zh: 3:1，新生儿不使用 AED

options.en: 5:1 with child AED pads in an anterior/posterior configuration
options.zh: 5:1，使用儿科电极片按前后位放置

questions.explanationEn: For a neonate (up to 28 days) the ratio is 3:1 and no AED is used. The ventilation-heavy ratio reflects that neonatal arrest is almost always respiratory in origin; shockable rhythms are so rare in this group that the AED has no role.
questions.explanationZh: 新生儿（出生 28 天内）按压通气比为 3:1，且不使用 AED。以通气为主的比例反映新生儿骤停几乎都源于呼吸问题；该人群可电击心律极为罕见，AED 无用武之地。

questions.questionEn: You deliver a baby who is floppy, limp, and not breathing, with a heart rate of 80. What is your first step under the newborn guideline?
questions.questionZh: 你接生的新生儿松软无力、无呼吸，心率 80。按 newborn 指南，第一步应做什么？

options.en: Start chest compressions immediately because the heart rate is below 100
options.zh: 因为心率低于 100，立即开始胸外按压

options.en: Ventilate with a BVM using 100% oxygen for 30 seconds
options.zh: 用 BVM 接 100% 氧气通气 30 秒

options.en: Apply an AED and analyze the rhythm
options.zh: 贴上 AED 并分析心律

options.en: Dry, stimulate, and keep the baby warm for 30 seconds, then reassess the heart rate
options.zh: 擦干、刺激并保暖 30 秒，然后复查心率

questions.explanationEn: Step 1 of the newborn sequence is dry, stimulate, and keep warm for 30 seconds; if the heart rate remains below 100 bpm you progress to step 2 (BVM on room air for 30 seconds), then step 3 (BVM with 100% oxygen for 30 seconds), and only then step 4, chest compressions, if the heart rate stays below 60. Many newborns respond to drying and stimulation alone.
questions.explanationZh: Newborn 流程第 1 步是擦干、刺激、保暖 30 秒；若心率仍低于 100 bpm 则进入第 2 步（室内空气 BVM 通气 30 秒），再到第 3 步（接 100% 氧气 BVM 通气 30 秒），只有心率仍低于 60 才进入第 4 步胸外按压。很多新生儿仅靠擦干和刺激就能恢复。

questions.questionEn: After 30 seconds of drying, stimulation, and warming, a newborn's heart rate is 88 bpm and he still is not breathing effectively. What is the next step?
questions.questionZh: 擦干、刺激、保暖 30 秒后，新生儿心率 88 bpm，仍无有效呼吸。下一步是什么？

options.en: Ventilate with a BVM on room air for 30 seconds, then reassess the heart rate
options.zh: 用 BVM 以室内空气通气 30 秒，然后复查心率

options.en: Begin chest compressions with ventilations at 3:1
options.zh: 以 3:1 开始按压加通气

options.en: Continue drying and stimulating for another 30 seconds
options.zh: 再继续擦干和刺激 30 秒

options.en: Attach 100% oxygen to the BVM immediately and ventilate
options.zh: 立即给 BVM 接 100% 氧气并通气

questions.explanationEn: Step 2 of the newborn sequence is ventilation with a BVM on room air for 30 seconds. Only if the heart rate remains below 100 bpm do you move to step 3 and attach 100% oxygen, and only if it remains below 100 after that do you begin compressions - which continue until the heart rate is above 60 bpm. Effective ventilation, not oxygen concentration, is the key intervention at this stage.
questions.explanationZh: Newborn 流程第 2 步是用 BVM 以室内空气通气 30 秒。只有心率仍低于 100 bpm 才进入第 3 步接 100% 氧气；仍低于 100 才开始胸外按压，并持续到心率高于 60 bpm。此阶段关键干预是有效通气，而不是氧浓度。

questions.questionEn: You have completed 30 seconds of BVM ventilation with 100% oxygen on a newborn. His heart rate is now 50 bpm. What should you do, and what is your endpoint?
questions.questionZh: 你已为新生儿用 BVM 接 100% 氧气通气 30 秒，现在心率 50 bpm。你应该怎么做？终点指标是什么？

options.en: Continue ventilations alone and reassess in 2 minutes
options.zh: 仅继续通气，2 分钟后复评

options.en: Begin chest compressions with ventilations and 100% oxygen, continuing until the heart rate is above 60 bpm
options.zh: 开始按压加通气并给 100% 氧气，持续到心率高于 60 bpm

options.en: Apply the AED and analyze before starting compressions
options.zh: 先贴 AED 分析心律再开始按压

options.en: Continue compressions until the heart rate exceeds 100 bpm, then stop ventilating
options.zh: 按压至心率超过 100 bpm 后停止通气

questions.explanationEn: Step 4 of the newborn sequence is chest compressions with ventilations and 100% oxygen until the heart rate is above 60 bpm. Note the two different thresholds: 100 bpm drives progression through the ventilation steps, while 60 bpm is the endpoint for compressions. No AED is used in neonates.
questions.explanationZh: Newborn 流程第 4 步是按压加通气并给 100% 氧气，直到心率高于 60 bpm。注意两个不同阈值：100 bpm 决定通气各步骤的推进，60 bpm 是停止按压的终点。新生儿不使用 AED。

questions.questionEn: For the purposes of the BC CPR guidelines, a patient is classified as a neonate up to what age?
questions.questionZh: 按 BC 的 CPR 指南，多大年龄以内的病人被归类为 neonate（新生儿）？

options.en: Up to 7 days
options.zh: 出生 7 天以内

options.en: Up to 12 hours
options.zh: 出生 12 小时以内

options.en: Up to 28 days
options.zh: 出生 28 天以内

options.en: Up to 1 year
options.zh: 出生 1 年以内

questions.explanationEn: The guideline defines a neonate as up to 28 days of age, with a 3:1 compression ratio and no AED. Beyond 28 days the patient is managed as an infant: brachial pulse check, 30:2 with one rescuer or 15:2 with two, and AED use as available.
questions.explanationZh: 指南将 neonate 定义为出生 28 天以内，采用 3:1 按压通气比且不使用 AED。超过 28 天则按婴儿处理：触诊肱动脉、单人 30:2 或双人 15:2，并按可用情况使用 AED。

questions.questionEn: Why is drying the newborn and maintaining warmth listed as part of the very first step of newborn resuscitation rather than an afterthought?
questions.questionZh: 为什么擦干新生儿和保暖被列为新生儿复苏的第一步内容，而不是事后再做的事？

options.en: It is done purely for the parents' comfort and reassurance
options.zh: 这纯粹是为了让父母安心舒适

options.en: Warmth only matters once the heart rate is above 100 bpm
options.zh: 只有心率超过 100 bpm 后保暖才有意义

options.en: Drying is primarily to allow the AED pads to adhere
options.zh: 擦干主要是为了让 AED 电极片能粘牢

options.en: A wet newborn loses heat extremely rapidly, and hypothermia worsens hypoxia and acidosis - drying also provides the stimulation that may itself restore effective breathing
options.zh: 湿身的新生儿散热极快，低体温会加重缺氧和酸中毒——而擦干本身提供的刺激就可能恢复有效呼吸

questions.explanationEn: Step 1 combines three actions for good reason: a wet newborn with a high surface-area-to-mass ratio cools within minutes, and hypothermia deepens hypoxia and acidosis, making resuscitation harder. The friction of drying is also the stimulation that frequently triggers effective respiration on its own. Neonates never receive an AED.
questions.explanationZh: 第 1 步把三个动作合在一起是有道理的：体表面积与体重比很高的湿身新生儿几分钟内就会失温，而低体温会加深缺氧和酸中毒，使复苏更困难。擦干时的摩擦本身也是刺激，常常能直接引发有效呼吸。新生儿不使用 AED。

questions.questionEn: A 3-week-old is brought to you limp, mottled, and hypothermic, with a heart rate of 55 and shallow irregular respirations. Which management set is correct?
questions.questionZh: 一名 3 周大的婴儿被送来时全身松软、皮肤花斑、体温偏低，心率 55，呼吸浅而不规则。哪一组处置是正确的？

options.en: Apply the AED first since bradycardia may indicate a shockable rhythm
options.zh: 先贴 AED——心动过缓可能提示可电击心律

options.en: Ventilate and begin compressions at a 3:1 ratio without an AED, keep him warm, and transport - at 21 days he is still a neonate
options.zh: 通气并以 3:1 开始按压、不用 AED、注意保暖并转运——21 天大仍属新生儿

options.en: Use 15:2 with two rescuers since he is over 2 weeks old
options.zh: 他已超过 2 周，双人施救应用 15:2

options.en: Give oxygen only and defer compressions until the heart rate falls below 40
options.zh: 只给氧，等心率降到 40 以下再开始按压

questions.explanationEn: At 21 days of age he is still within the 28-day neonatal definition, so the 3:1 ratio applies and no AED is used. Bradycardia below 60 with poor perfusion is an indication to start compressions - not to wait for a lower number - and warming matters because hypothermia both causes and worsens neonatal deterioration.
questions.explanationZh: 21 天大仍在 28 天的新生儿定义范围内，因此适用 3:1 比例且不使用 AED。心率低于 60 且灌注不良就是开始按压的指征——不能等到更低的数值——保暖同样重要，因为低体温既是新生儿恶化的原因也会使其加重。

questions.questionEn: You assist a delivery. After drying and stimulation the baby cries vigorously, has good tone, and her heart rate is 140. What is your management?
questions.questionZh: 你协助完成一次接生。擦干和刺激后婴儿大声啼哭、肌张力良好，心率 140。你的处置是什么？

options.en: No ventilation or compressions are needed - keep her warm and dry, monitor breathing, tone, and heart rate, and transport mother and baby together
options.zh: 不需要通气或按压——保持温暖干燥，监测呼吸、肌张力和心率，母婴一同转运

options.en: Begin BVM ventilation on room air for 30 seconds as a precaution
options.zh: 为保险起见，先用室内空气 BVM 通气 30 秒

options.en: Start compressions at 3:1 because all newborns require initial support
options.zh: 以 3:1 开始按压——所有新生儿都需要初始支持

options.en: Apply the AED to establish a baseline rhythm
options.zh: 贴 AED 以取得基线心律

questions.explanationEn: The newborn resuscitation sequence is triggered by a baby who is floppy, limp, not breathing, or has a heart rate below 100 bpm. A vigorous crying baby with good tone and a heart rate of 140 meets none of those, so she needs only warmth, drying, and ongoing observation of breathing, tone, and heart rate. Unnecessary ventilation and compressions cause harm, and neonates never receive an AED.
questions.explanationZh: 新生儿复苏流程的启动条件是：松软无力、无呼吸，或心率低于 100 bpm。大声啼哭、肌张力良好、心率 140 的婴儿都不符合，因此只需保暖、擦干，并持续观察呼吸、肌张力和心率。不必要的通气和按压会造成伤害，而新生儿从不使用 AED。
